data.title: Show HN: Jobs by Referral: Find jobs in your LinkedIn network
data.author: nicksergeant
data.article_summary:
JobsByReferral.com帮助用户通过LinkedIn网络寻找工作机会。它通过分析用户下载的LinkedIn数据，找到用户 connections 所在公司的职位空缺，从而增加被推荐和获得面试的机会。具体步骤包括：

1. 下载LinkedIn数据档案（通过“数据隐私”设置获取完整数据，包括Connections.csv文件）。
2. 可选择使用demo数据体验功能。
3. 上传LinkedIn数据文件（ZIP格式或Connections.csv文件）开始搜索。

该工具旨在利用已有的人脉网络，提高求职成功率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LinkedIn网络内搜索功能及其相关问题

不同观点：
• Gergely和Floutist44认为LinkedIn已经存在"在你的网络中"的搜索过滤功能，且该功能已使用多年，新的AI搜索只是让这个功能更加智能化。
• Hackernewds对该功能表示赞赏，认为这是LinkedIn早就应该开发的功能。
• 1970-01-01指出，有些人虽然保留LinkedIn档案，但并不活跃，因此该功能可能不完全有效。
• Thih9关注个人数据隐私问题，询问数据是否被存储或用于其他目的，是否有隐私政策保护用户数据。
• B8提到在其他平台如Blind上可以获得推荐，但质疑LinkedIn上随机添加的人是否会真正提供推荐。
• Fuzzy1000建议增加一个功能，可以精确定位和分析人际网络中的连接。
• Orliesaurus将这个功能比作Blind的升级版。
• Dijit提出相反的需求，希望有一个推荐之前共事过的优秀同事给当前公司的功能，并描述了自己曾经尝试开发该功能的经历。
• Shados认为这个功能展示了AI将如何彻底改变行业，并讨论了LinkedIn内部可能的产品开发流程，强调外部开发者能更快实现新功能。
• Bsoles关注数据安全问题，引用LinkedIn要求用户下载和提供整个LinkedIn数据的做法，提出担忧。
• Toyg对功能实现方式提出质疑，认为这是在让用户进行LinkedIn数据抓取，建议使用官方API，并指出该服务在GDPR合规性上的重大影响。

补充讨论：
• 数据隐私和合规性是讨论中的一个重要问题，特别是对于欧洲用户的GDPR合规性。
• 功能的实现方式引起了一些争议，特别是关于使用官方API和用户数据抓取的问题。
• 对功能的实际效果和用户使用习惯存在不同看法，例如对不活跃用户档案的过滤效果和推荐的真实性。

data.title: Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna – Nuclear propulsion and solar sailing
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了利用先进推进技术前往太阳系边缘天体塞德娜的可行性。研究评估了两种推进方案：基于D-³He热核聚变的直接融合驱动（DFD）火箭引擎，以及利用涂层热脱附进行推进的太阳帆。对于DFD方案，分析假设了一个1.6兆瓦的系统，能够实现约10年抵达塞德娜，其中包括1.5年的持续推力。而对于太阳帆，则考虑通过木星引力辅助进行飞越，预计7年完成任务。研究还考虑了有效载荷能力、旅行时间、科学回报以及通信限制等关键参数。结果为未来深空探测任务规划提供了基础对比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sedna探测任务的可行性及相关推进技术（尤其是直接融合驱动技术）的发展现状和前景

不同观点：
• **pavel_lishin** 对Direct Fusion Drive（DFD）的实际进展表示怀疑，特别是其可靠性和能否在太空长时间运行。同时指出，鉴于Sedna的轨道特性，传统推进系统需要长达30年的深空旅行，因此任务需要尽快启动。
• **myrmidon** 认为DFD是一个有趣的概念，可能为未来的星际旅行提供可能性，但对DFD如何选择D/He3融合而不是D/D融合表示困惑，并担心中子辐射问题。
• **mikewarot** 提到了过去的核裂变项目（如Project Rover），认为近期的核系统可能更可行，并指出在轨的OTP-2卫星已经使用了创新的推进系统，包括“融合增强”的离子推进器。
• **stevenAthompson** 提出了一种替代方案，建议发射大量小型网状探测器，利用数量优势和低成本（类似手机成本）来弥补单个探测器的性能不足。
• **pier25** 认为即使使用DFD，到达Sedna也需要长达40年的时间线，质疑是否有组织能够长期维持这样的项目预算和规划。
• **jmyeet** 对所有提到的推进技术持怀疑态度，认为目前的技术都处于非常初期的阶段，尚未经过实际验证，特别是核推进技术。此外，对长时间任务中探测器的生存能力和太阳帆的耐久性表示担忧，并建议将资源投入到天王星或海王星的探测任务中。

补充讨论：
• **accrual** 认为Sedna的远距离探测可能揭示其表面分子的意外信息，有助于理解其起源和远处的太空环境。
• **ananddtyagi** 以《三体》小说作类比，暗示任务的复杂性和科幻性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于当前推进技术（尤其是DFD）的实际可行性和成熟度，以及长时间深空任务中探测器的生存能力与任务规划的现实性。

Title:
Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna -- Nuclear propulsion and advanced solar sailing concepts
Authors:
Elena Ancona
,
Roman Ya. Kezerashvili
,
Savino Longo
View a PDF of the paper titled Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna -- Nuclear propulsion and advanced solar sailing concepts, by Elena Ancona and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Exploring the outer reaches of the Solar System presents significant propulsion and mission design challenges. This study assesses the feasibility of a mission to Sedna using two advanced propulsion concepts: the Direct Fusion Drive (DFD) rocket engine, based on D-$^{3}$He thermonuclear fusion, and a solar sail utilizing thermal desorption of its coating for propulsion. Both are evaluated for a one-way Earth-to-Sedna mission; however, due to the different performances the DFD would enable orbit insertion, whereas for the solar sail a flyby is envisioned. The analysis evaluates key mission parameters, including delivered payload capacity, travel time, and potential science return. For the DFD, we assume a 1.6 MW system with constant thrust and specific impulse, while for the solar sail, we consider acceleration via thermal desorption and a gravity-assist maneuver around Jupiter. The mission analysis incorporates four key phases: departure, interplanetary acceleration, interplanetary coasting, and rendezvous. Sedna is expected to pass through the perihelion of its orbit in 2075--2076 and then move again away from the Sun. Considering the distances involved, a mission targeting the object would need to be launched "relatively" soon, especially if using conventional propulsion systems, which could require up to 30 years of deep-space travel. In our study, results indicate that the DFD could reach Sedna in approximately 10 years, with 1.5 years of thrusting, while the solar sail, assisted by Jupiter's gravity, could complete the journey in 7 years. The feasibility of science payload accommodation, power availability, and communication constraints is also considered. These findings provide a comparative foundation for future deep-space mission planning.

data.author: adilhafeez

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一篇论文中提出方法的实际应用和效果的讨论

不同观点：
• [sparacha] 作为论文的合著者，愿意回答有关其方法的任何问题，表现出开放讨论的态度。
• [pseudosavant] 关注该方法对请求延迟的影响，特别是通过代理时的延迟问题，暗示了对实际应用中性能的关心。
• [jgant13] 询问何时使用该方法而不是OpenRouter，显示出对不同工具选择标准的兴趣，特别是性能方面的比较。
• [tmaly] 提出关于模型量化的问题，关心在保持良好结果的前提下是否可以实现模型的量化。
• [_nh_] 要求与RouteLLM进行比较，显示出对该方法相对于其他类似工具的竞争力的关注。
• [jedisct1] 分享了实际使用体验，指出在特定任务（评级编码任务难度）中，该方法的表现不如Qwen2.5-Coder-7B，暗示了模型规模和性能之间的关系。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是该方法在实际应用中的性能表现，特别是在与其他工具和模型的比较中。
• 讨论还涉及模型的技术细节，如量化和规模对性能的影响，表明读者对实际部署中的技术实现细节有深入兴趣。
• 不同评论者根据各自的使用场景提出了具体问题和反馈，显示出对该方法在多样化应用场景中的实用性的关注。

data.title: Show HN: Core – open source memory graph for LLMs – shareable, user owned
data.author: Manik_agg
data.article_summary:
C.O.R.E（Contextual Observation & Recall Engine）是一个为大型语言模型（LLM）提供的个人记忆层，用户拥有完全控制权，可本地运行或使用托管版本，并与其他工具（如Cursor、Claude）连接以共享上下文。其核心功能包括：

1. 提供私密的个人记忆图谱，数据本地存储，跨应用访问。
2. 帮助AI助手（如SOL）获取用户上下文，提供个性化响应。
3. 动态知识图谱，记录事实的全历史，支持透明追溯。
4. 支持实时审计和变更追踪，例如价格变更或项目进展。

C.O.R.E.
Contextual Observation & Recall Engine
C.O.R.E is a shareable memory for LLMs which is private, portable and 100% owned by the user. You can either run it locally or use our hosted version and then connect with other tools like Cursor, Claude to share your context at multiple places.
C.O.R.E is built for two reasons:
To give you complete ownership of your memory, stored locally and accessible across any app needing LLM context.
To help SOL (your AI assistant) access your context, facts, and preferences for more relevant and personalized responses.
Note:
We are actively working on improving support for Llama models. At the moment, C.O.R.E does not provide optimal results with Llama-based models, but we are making progress to ensure better compatibility and output in the near future.
Demo Video
Check C.O.R.E Demo
How is C.O.R.E different from other Memory Providers?
Unlike most memory systems—which act like basic sticky notes, only showing what’s true right now. C.O.R.E is built as a dynamic, living temporal knowledge graph:
Every fact is a first-class “Statement” with full history, not just a static edge between entities.
Each statement includes what was said, who said it, when it happened, and why it matters.
You get full transparency: you can always trace the source, see what changed, and explore why the system “believes” something.
Use Case Example: Real Change Auditing
Imagine you ask SOL: "What changed in our pricing since Q1?"
With C.O.R.E, you see exactly what prices changed, who approved them, the context (meeting, email, document), and when each update happened—enabling true compliance, auditability, and insight across products, teams, and time.
Or ask: “What does Mike know about Project Phoenix?” and get a timeline of meetings, decisions, and facts Mike was involved in, with full traceability to those specific events.

Use Docker Compose to start all required services:
docker-compose up
Access the App
Once the containers are running, open your browser and go to
http://localhost:3000
.
Login with Magic Link
Choose the "Magic Link" login option.
Enter your email.
Copy the magic link from terminal logs and open it in your browser.
Create Your Private Space & Ingest Data
In the dashboard, go to the ingest section.
Type a message, e.g.,
I love playing badminton
, and click "Add".
Your memory is queued for processing; you can monitor its status in the server logs.
Once processing is complete, nodes will be added to your private knowledge graph and visible in the dashboard.
You can later choose to connect this memory to other tools or keep it private.
Search Your Memory
Use the dashboard's search feature to query your ingested data within your private space.

data.title: The wanton destruction of a creative-tech era
data.author: gregsadetsky
data.article_summary: 这篇文章激烈批评了Fastly公司决定关闭Glitch.com的决定。Glitch是一个让人们创作、分享和灵感碰撞的网站，因其社区和创意环境受到喜爱。作者指责Fastly为了商业利益背弃了用户信任，制造了大量的404错误页面，并可能损害其在CDN市场的声誉。文章充满了讽刺和愤怒，表达了对Glitch关闭的深切失望和悲痛，并调侃地提出以表演和个人牺牲换取延长关闭时间的建议。最终，作者认为这种决定是无情的企业行为，忽视了用户的感受和社区的价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Glitch平台关闭的原因及其影响

不同观点：
• **pseudosavant**：对Glitch的关闭感到遗憾，但承认该平台缺乏商业模式，用户不付费导致无法持续运营。他提到已将工具迁移到GitHub Pages，虽然迭代速度较慢，但依然能满足需求。他还分享了自己使用在线VS Code编辑代码的经验。

• **robotnikman**：引用一句话，暗示创造价值和坚持价值观之间存在矛盾，对Glitch的关闭表达了情感上的触动。

• **bruce511**：指出用户和顾客的区别，认为用户往往希望产品免费，而顾客（如风投公司）才实际支付账单。他认为，依赖风投资金的公司会优先考虑顾客（投资者）的满意度，而非单纯用户的满意度。他强调，免费用户抱怨产品关闭是认知失调的表现，因为不付费就无法保证产品的长久生存。

• **monster_truck**：认为很多真诚的Glitch用户没有意识到平台被滥用的问题，尽管平台团队已经尽力维护。这暗示了平台关闭可能与管理问题和滥用行为有关。

• **chaosprint**：对Glitch的关闭表示悲伤，回忆了在该平台上创作的艺术作品。他提到用户正在向Netlify和Cloudflare等其他平台迁移。

补充讨论：
• **平台迁移**：多个评论提到了用户将项目迁移到其他平台（如GitHub Pages、Netlify、Cloudflare），表明这些平台可能是Glitch的替代选项。

• **商业模式与生存**：讨论中多次提到商业模式对平台生存的重要性，指出免费用户不付费对平台长期生存的影响，以及风投公司对公司决策的影响。

争议焦点：
• 用户期望与商业现实之间的矛盾：用户希望平台免费，但平台需要盈利才能生存。这种认知失调是讨论中的一个争议点。

44437015.article_content:
Fastly, you killed glitch.com and ruined your karma for 10,000 years. You have “
betrayed yourself for nothing
.”
Glitch was an idealistic place where people gathered and made sites, were inspired by other people’s sites and remixed them, and generally enjoyed themselves. Of course a site like that takes money to run, of course you need people to run it - it was specifically better because of the people that ran it. And I can only be very sympathetic to the fact that it cost money - that it only existed because of money - and maybe the reality of that site ever existing was a mirage. Maybe we never deserved a place that made creation easy, maybe a community of people who loved to work together and share should never have existed. Maybe it would have been better if we never cared! That would have been easier and cheaper too. I’m sorry anyone ever felt happy there.
But you gutless monsters bought it - you spent money on it. Why? Venture capital back-dealing? Friends of friends of friends of friends back-scratching? Someone somewhere had to cash out on
their
investment, so here’s a nice public company that will end up making good on everyone’s past rounds? I have no clue! Maybe someone at Fastly actually believed in Glitch for an honest nanosecond but then changed their minds. Which led to this extraordinary linkicide - yes, my beautiful Fastly babies, you just smothered the web with millions of 404s all pointing back to you. Will all future dead Glitch urls redirect to https://www.fastly.com/contact-sales ?
I hope that when every LLM starts answering questions like “what’s the best enterprise cdn” and “what’s the most reliable cdn” or “where should I host my cdn I am the president of pharma”, you show up as an alternative not worthy of trust. “Fastly has been shown to abandon millions of sites without a care in the world, telling users and customers that they have a month to get the most absolutely fucking furthest out of the way. You should not consider them for your Fortune 1000.”
No but truly, I’m sorry. 99.8% of the people involved - Fastly employees, fans, supporters, users - had nothing to do with this. This is malice that could only have come from an enterprise executive. A committee maybe? It would honestly feel better if this was some sort of firing by LLM. Did ChatGPT make you a slide deck called “this quarter’s misery” and grouped the killing of Glitch with other smart cost saving measures such as LED lightbulbs and single ply toilet paper? You guys rock. Saving money, creating shareholder value… It’s easy to create value when you don’t have values.
Could I buy a single 6.98 USD stock (actual current price, ouch I shouldn’t have looked at that Google Finance graph, I almost started feeling bad) and show up at a shareholder event? Could I performatively dance the pain of millions of sites dying? Would you watch? Would you cry - do you remember how?
Yes, in this beautiful messy world of wars, famine and raw milk detoxfluencers, the ending of an internet website host ranks as a LOW priority. It should not be on anyone’s radar. It is a reality that we should ignore. They’re just feelings, and feelings are not real. Life goes by. “
Ars longa, vita brevis
”, except if your Ars is hosted by Fastly. Then your Ars will be extra, extra brevis.
Fastly, my loves, have you considered shame?
xx
P.s. I am SO not blackmailing you, but if you extended the Glitch shutdown date by, like, two years, I will write a beautiful retraction, I will drink a gallon of raw milk and I will stream it all live for your sadistic pleasure. Consider it a deal. 🤝.

data.title: Soldier’s wrist purse discovered at Roman legionary camp
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 考古学家在捷克南摩拉维亚的一处临时罗马军营遗址中发现了一名士兵的腕包碎片。该军营由驻扎于公元172至180年间第10军团建立，时值马科曼尼战争。腕包设计独特，佩戴在左臂上，右臂则可自由战斗。虽然包内未发现钱币，但同一考古环境中出土了大量罗马硬币。专家推测，腕包可容纳约50枚银德纳里，接近罗马士兵的年薪。此发现展示了罗马军队后勤的复杂性，并为研究帝国边境士兵生活提供了实物证据。目前，该腕包在穆肖夫游客中心展出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对考古发现的钱包重建物品的分析和感受

不同观点：
• [cyrusmg] 认为有更好的照片可以展示该物品，提供了一个链接以查看其他角度的照片。

44406401.article_content:
Image Credit : Václav Šálek, ČTK
By:
Mark Milligan
Date:
June 27, 2025
Archaeology
Soldier’s wrist purse discovered at Roman legionary camp
Archaeologists have discovered a fragment of a soldier’s wrist purse at the site of a temporary Roman camp in South Moravia, Czech Republic.
The camp was established by the 10th Legion, who was stationed in the area between AD 172 and 180 during the Marcomannic Wars, a campaign against the Germanic Marcomanni, the Quadi, and the Sarmatian Iazyges.
- Advertisement -
The find is especially significant because it was uncovered outside the traditional boundaries of the Roman Empire. “It is quite like a small moneybox,” explains Balázs Komoróczy of the Czech Academy of Sciences.
“It was held on the arm or forearm, where tension closed and held it tight.” The design indicates that it would be worn on the left arm, leaving the right hand free for fighting.
No coins were found inside the purse itself, but a large quantity of Roman coinage was found from the same archaeological context. Experts suggest that the purse could hold as much as 50 silver denarii, just short of a yearly salary for a Roman legionary.
The bronze purse likely held soldiers’ private funds and “service cash,” which was used to finance operational expenses such as rations and equipment. Its discovery not only testifies to the logistical complexity of Roman army campaigns but also presents a tangible glimpse into soldiers’ existence on the empire’s frontier in transition.
- Advertisement -
The purse is currently on display at the Pasohlávky-based Mušov Visitor Centre, where visitors can view the fragment, a highly detailed reconstruction, and part of the coins found in the nearby context.

主要讨论点：QUIC和HTTP3技术的应用和推广情况，以及相关工具库的成熟度和可用性

不同观点：
• [ycombinatrix] 认为通过移除某些部分（如Vec）可以使代码与no_std环境兼容，关注点在于技术实现的细节，尤其是兼容性问题。

• [jauntywundrkind] 承认定制的多路复用协议工具包可能有优势，但表达了对QUIC和HTTP3技术未能广泛普及的失望。具体提到：
  - QUIC和HTTP3目前仍未被主流采用，尽管一些大公司有自己的库，但缺乏易用的、与HTTP框架结合良好的HTTP3解决方案。
  - 提到Hyper的h3项目进展缓慢，以及Node.js在QUIC实现上的困难，特别是与OpenSSL相关的问题。
  - 对QUIC技术的社会关注度和开发努力不足表示遗憾，认为QUIC可以替代许多定制的解决方案，并提到Apache Iggy作为一个早期但性能良好的QUIC消息传递工具。

补充讨论：
• QUIC和HTTP3的潜在价值：[jauntywundrkind] 强调QUIC的通用性和对各种应用传输的巨大升级潜力，认为其可以替代许多现有的定制解决方案。

• 具体项目和工具的状态：[jauntywundrkind] 引用了多个具体项目和问题跟踪链接，如Hyper的h3项目和Node.js的相关问题，来说明目前QUIC和HTTP3工具库的进展和存在的问题。

争议焦点：
• QUIC和HTTP3技术的主流采用和普及程度：[jauntywundrkind] 对QUIC和HTTP3技术未能广泛普及表示失望和不满，而[ycombinatrix] 则没有直接涉及这一问题，更关注技术实现的细节。

• 技术实现和兼容性：[ycombinatrix] 关注代码的no_std兼容性问题，而[jauntywundrkind] 更关注技术的社会普及和应用情况。

data.title: Give footnotes the boot – alternatives to footnotes on the web
data.author: jaffathecake
data.article_summary: 本文批评了脚注在印刷和网络媒体中的使用，认为脚注破坏了阅读的连贯性，尤其是在网络上使用时更加不便。在印刷品中，脚注需要读者中断阅读去查看页脚，而在网络上，读者可能需要滚动到文章末尾，甚至在视觉上寻找相关脚注。尽管超链接可以改善这一点，但许多作者仍使用无意义的数字作为链接文本，造成困惑和小点击区域。文章建议，替代脚注的方法可以是使用括号插入简短补充内容，或通过`<section role="note">`元素提供更长但易于阅读的补充信息。作者呼吁放弃脚注，采用更好的方式来提供补充内容，以提升用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页脚注/旁注/尾注的设计与实现

不同观点：
• **wonger_** 支持使用非超链接的脚注，让读者自行滚动查看，认为这样可以减少干扰和避免可访问性问题。他还提到了几种实现方式，包括Dorian的可扩展括号和Gwern的旁注实现。
• **paradox460** 在自己网站上使用旁注，并在页面空间足够时将脚注显示在页面旁边，提供悬停效果以增加用户体验。同时，考虑为移动端添加弹出式旁注，但因UX问题尚未实现。
• **dado3212** 偏好使用CSS实现旁注，不依赖JavaScript，桌面端旁注可以弹出显示，移动端则直接内联显示，避免跳转。
• **nicbou** 在其网站上大量使用脚注，主要用于引用来源。虽然脚注标记可能分散注意力并影响复制文本，但数字形式效果最佳。
• **jt2190** 批评文章没有先明确问题就讨论解决方案，认为脚注不应包含“更多要说”的内容，而是提供对部分读者有用的额外信息，同时不必拘泥于印刷品的传统方式。
• **account42** 批评某篇文章正文的字号过大，甚至其脚注的字号也偏大。
• **egypturnash** 指出电子书普遍使用尾注而非脚注，对此表示不满，认为脚注应在同一页底部展示。
• **theandrewbailey** 提到使用“点击这里”作为链接文本的问题，并引用了Aaron Swartz的建议作为参考。
• **globular-toast** 质疑阅读脚注是否真的困难，表示自己从未遇到问题。
• **JadeNB** 支持使用带有返回锚点的脚注，以提供熟悉的阅读体验，并提到Daring Fireball网站的实现方式。
• **lorenzohess** 批评原作者未适当评估“弹出式”脚注的解决方案，并详细比较了弹出式与作者提出的三种替代方案，认为弹出式是最优解，且其他方案存在多种问题，如增加干扰、占用空间、不易复制等。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于脚注、旁注和尾注的最佳实现方式，尤其是在桌面端和移动端不同设备上的表现。
• 不同用户对脚注的干扰程度、可访问性、视觉效果等有不同看法，反映了设计中需要权衡的多个方面。
• 有人关注具体实现的技术细节，如CSS与JavaScript的使用、链接目标的尺寸与易用性等。
• 对脚注内容是否应包含“更多要说”的信息及其与主文本的关系也有不同理解。

44436984.article_content:
Give footnotes the boot
Posted 01 July 2025
I hate footnotes
1
, and hopefully by the end of this, you will too. Let's get down to it…
The UX of footnotes in printed media
You, the reader, encounter a tiny number
2
within some prose. This indicates to you that I, the writer, have something more to say on this topic. And, for your inconvenience, I've put it way down at the bottom of the page.
The choice is yours: do you skip over it, and stay in the flow of the article, or do you set off on a side-quest to discover the extra wisdom I have to offer?
It's like one of those "choose your own adventure" books, except you know the destination is a dead-end, meaning you'll have to re-trace your steps so you can continue the main thread of the article.
Maybe if you know me well enough, you can be in tune with the kinds of things that I'd choose to leave in a footnote, and you can make some kind of judgement on whether it's likely to be worth your time. But since this is the first time I've used footnotes in an article
3
, you don't really have anything to go on. All that little 3 tells you is that there's some additional content that may or may not be contextually useful to you, and that it's the third time I've done this to you.
Whether you go out of your way to read the footnote content is really just a test of your curiosity.
If you did make your way down to the footnotes, I hope you appreciated that I set the text size to be a little smaller than the 'ideal' size that I chose for the main body content, making them harder to read, such is the tradition within the footnote community.
And if you enjoyed all of that, I have
great news for you
: many people bring this experience to the world wide web.
Footnotes on the web
If reproduced as-is, footnotes on the web are even worse than their printed counterparts. In print, the footnotes are usually at the bottom of the current page, so they're a quick glance away, and you can use a finger to mark your place in the main text while you're off on your side-quest. Whereas on this beautiful pageless web of ours, you have to scroll all the way down to the end of the article. You can try flinging right to the bottom of the document, but if there's a sizeable footer or comments section, you'll overshoot the footnotes. And of course, after all of this, you have to scroll back to where you were, which is easier said than done.
However, most webby footnoters have realised that in the printed world, the numbering of footnotes is used to manually
link
the primary content to the supplemental content, and the web has a dedicated feature to enhance connections like this: hyperlinks
4
.
Of course, with footnotes being at the bottom of the article, sometimes these links will simply take you to the end of the document, so you'll
still
have to visually scan for the pertinent footnote
5
.
If the footnote markers are links, then the user can use the back button/gesture to return to the main content. But, even though this restores the previous scroll position, the user is still left with the challenge of finding their previous place in a wall of text
6
.
We could try to solve that problem by dynamically pulling the content from the footnotes and displaying it in a popover. In some browsers
that will display like a tooltip, pointing directly back to the footnote marker. Thanks to modern web features, this can be done entirely without JavaScript
7
.
But this is still shit! I see good, smart people, who'd always
avoid using "click here" as link text
, littering their articles with link texts such as
1
,
7
, and
sometimes even
12
. Not only is this as contextless as "click here", it also provides the extra frustration of a tiny-weeny hit target.
And all this for what? To cargo-cult academia? Stop it! Stop it now! Footnotes are a shitty hack built on the limitations of printed media. It's dumb to build on top of those limitations when they don't exist on the web platform. So I ask you to break free of footnotes and do something better.
Alternatives to footnotes on the web
Here are the goals:
Provide easily-read supplementary content.
Let the user easily skip over it if they're not interested.
Make it easy for the user to decide if they're interested or not.
Given that:
Just, like… parentheses?
Honestly, if you've got a quick little aside, just pop it in parentheses. If the reader really wants to skip it, scanning for the next closing parenthesis is pretty easy (unless you're nesting them – don't do that), and it keeps the reader in the flow of the article.
A 'note' section
If your content is a little longer, you can use
<section role="note">
and style it to look self-contained.
Why not
<aside>
?
I thought
the
<aside>
element
would be ideal for this, but that uses
the
complementary
role
which doesn't seem like a good fit for this kind of content. Whereas
the
note
role
is specifically for "parenthetic or ancillary content", which sounds perfect.

• **theandrewbailey** 提到使用“点击这里”作为链接文本的问题，并引用了Aaron Swartz的建议作为参考。
• **globular-toast** 质疑阅读脚注是否真的困难，表示自己从未遇到问题。
• **JadeNB** 支持使用带有返回锚点的脚注，以提供熟悉的阅读体验，并提到Daring Fireball网站的实现方式。
• **lorenzohess** 批评原作者未适当评估“弹出式”脚注的解决方案，并详细比较了弹出式与作者提出的三种替代方案，认为弹出式是最优解，且其他方案存在多种问题，如增加干扰、占用空间、不易复制等。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于脚注、旁注和尾注的最佳实现方式，尤其是在桌面端和移动端不同设备上的表现。
• 不同用户对脚注的干扰程度、可访问性、视觉效果等有不同看法，反映了设计中需要权衡的多个方面。
• 有人关注具体实现的技术细节，如CSS与JavaScript的使用、链接目标的尺寸与易用性等。
• 对脚注内容是否应包含“更多要说”的信息及其与主文本的关系也有不同理解。

主要讨论点：评论围绕一篇关于朝鲜战争及其遗留影响的文章展开，涉及文章中的隐喻、科学描述、文章标题及内容准确性、以及对朝鲜非军事区（DMZ）的讨论。

不同观点：
• **文章隐喻的理解**：
   - [octaane] 认为文章用麻雀 metaphor 描述因朝鲜战争而流离失所的韩国人及其后代，强调读过文章的人能够理解这一点。
   - [sim7c00] 也提到文章通过隐喻将鸟类与人类经历联系起来，尽管起初以为文章只关于鸟类，但对文章产生兴趣并愿意进一步了解韩国历史。

• **对科学描述的质疑**：
   - [shellfishgene] 对文章中提到的河口功能表示怀疑，认为如果河口真的能将盐水净化成为淡水流入国家，那将非常“了不起”，并询问是否理解有误。

• **标题的准确性**：
   - [1317] 提出文章标题不够准确，建议更准确的标题应为《战争的遗留与跨越朝鲜非军事区的河口》。

• **对DMZ的讨论和疑问**：
   - [bux93] 惊讶地发现文章暗示DMZ内有居民，并提出许多问题，如DMZ内是否真的有永久居民，以及提到的南北韩村庄的真实情况。
   - [ggm] 提到DMZ不仅是军事区，也是野生动物的绿洲，并指出野生动物作为隐喻，象征希望。

补充讨论：
• **情感共鸣**：
   - [kwoff] 引用了文章中的情感片段，描述了一个关于“实乡民”（실향민）和“燕子”（제비）的故事，表达了对流离失所者的情感共鸣。

• **幽默与调侃**：
   - [analog31] 和 [saretup] 以幽默的方式提到了与“燕子”相关的其他文化背景（如“Capistrano”和“非洲或欧洲燕子”），属于轻松调侃。
   - [DonHopkins] 和 [salvage7111] 继续以幽默方式讨论“燕子”和“吞蝇的老太太”，属于无关主旨的幽默插曲。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于文章中科学描述的真实性，特别是河口功能的描述，[shellfishgene] 对此表示怀疑并提出问题。
• 对DMZ内是否有居民存在疑问，[bux93] 对此提出质疑并希望得到更多信息。

data.title: Show HN: I made a 2D game engine in Dart
data.author: joemanaco
data.article_summary: Bullseye2D是一个为Dart语言设计的高性能2D游戏库，具有简单易用的API和快速的WebGL渲染器，开发者可以快速上手制作游戏。它支持2D图形渲染、多种输入处理（键盘、手柄、触屏等）、音频播放与控制、资源管理等功能，并且提供核心版（MIT许可）的免费使用和高级版（开发中）的赞助计划。核心版包含制作和发布游戏的所有基本功能，而高级版将引入场景管理、精灵动画、高级碰撞检测等强大特性。赞助者可获得高级版的早期访问权及其他特权。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个新的Dart语言2D游戏库（Bullseye）的发布及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• **支持与期待**：一些用户对该项目表示支持和期待，如[sgt]表示对项目的看好并可能提供赞助，[rcore]和[munificent]则对新游戏引擎的发布表示赞赏和喜爱。

• **对项目宣传语言的质疑**：[leecommamichael]认为项目宣传中声称的“易用、高性能”缺乏具体的衡量标准和相对比较，认为这些描述更多是为了吸引注意，而非提供实质性信息。

• **与其他工具的比较**：[_stillmind]提到已有的Flame引擎，并希望了解Bullseye相对于Flame的优势和不足，建议通过具体教程对比来展示其独特之处。

• **对项目功能的问题**：[devrandoom]注意到Boing游戏不支持手机，质疑这是否是设计上的决定。

• **对Dart语言的疑问**：[socalgal2]对Dart语言的吸引力提出疑问，希望了解Dart相比其他语言的特殊之处和优势。

• **对项目展示的批评**：[zxexz]批评主页上缺乏截图或演示，认为这是不足之处。

争议焦点：
• **宣传语言的实质性**：部分用户如[leecommamichael]对项目宣传中的模糊描述表示不满，认为需要更具体的比较和衡量标准。

data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 这篇论文通过玻尔兹曼 kinetic 理论，从刚性球形粒子系统的弹性碰撞出发，严格推导出流体力学中的基本偏微分方程（PDEs），如可压缩欧拉方程和不可压缩纳维-斯托克斯-傅里叶方程。这解决了希尔伯特第六问题中从牛顿定律出发推导流体方程的课题。证明基于在二维和三维环面上推导玻尔兹曼方程，扩展了作者之前的工作（arXiv:2408.07818）。论文全长48页，包含5个图表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇论文的评价及其在物理学中的意义

不同观点：
• [ngriffiths] 引用了John Baez在Mastodon上的讨论，指出虽然Shan Gao的评论认为该论文有一些不错的成果，但问题仍未完全解决。Baez认为该论文提出了有价值的工作，但问题仍然是开放的。
• [rnhmjoj] 质疑论文的创新性，认为推导Boltzmann方程和流体方程在等离子体物理教科书中是常见内容，且可以通过Liouville定理和BBGKY层级进行推导，暗示该论文可能缺乏新意。
• [LudwigNagasena] 提出更深层次的问题，关注从对称可逆方程到湍流不可逆性之间的转变是如何发生的，这可能涉及对论文中未详细讨论的物理现象的进一步探讨。

补充讨论：
• [IdealeZahlen] 提供了一个视频链接，Sabine Hossenfelder的视频可能对理解论文的背景和意义有所帮助。
• [whatshisface] 提供了一个更大的工作链接，指出该论文可能是这一更大工作的一部分，试图提供更多背景以理解论文的重要性。
• [quantadev] 的评论被标记，没有实质性内容。

争议焦点：
• 论文的创新性和其在物理学领域的贡献是讨论的主要争议点。一方认为论文提出了开放性问题，有其价值；另一方则认为其内容在现有教科书中已有详细讨论，缺乏新意。

Abstract:
In this paper, we rigorously derive the fundamental PDEs of fluid mechanics, such as the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations, starting from the hard sphere particle systems undergoing elastic collisions. This resolves Hilbert's sixth problem, as it pertains to the program of deriving the fluid equations from Newton's laws by way of Boltzmann's kinetic theory. The proof relies on the derivation of Boltzmann's equation on 2D and 3D tori, which is an extension of our previous work (
arXiv:2408.07818
).

data.title: Huawei releases an open weight model trained on Huawei Ascend GPUs
data.author: buyucu
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Pangu Pro MoE的混合专家模型（Mixture of Grouped Experts, MoGE），旨在提高大规模语言模型的计算效率。传统MoE模型中，不同专家被激活的频率不均，导致计算负载不平衡。MoGE通过将专家分组并限制每组中被激活的专家数量，实现了更均衡的计算负载分配，尤其在多设备运行时表现优异。Pangu Pro MoE基于Ascend NPUs构建，总参数为720亿，每次激活160亿参数。实验表明，MoGE在训练和推理阶段均提升了效率，推理速度达1148 tokens/s，通过加速可提升至1528 tokens/s，优于同类密集模型。该设计显著改善了计算性能和成本效益。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The surgence of Mixture of Experts (MoE) in Large Language Models promises a small price of execution cost for a much larger model parameter count and learning capacity, because only a small fraction of parameters are activated for each input token. However, it is commonly observed that some experts are activated far more often than others, leading to system inefficiency when running the experts on different devices in parallel. Therefore, we introduce Mixture of Grouped Experts (MoGE), which groups the experts during selection and balances the expert workload better than MoE in nature. It constrains tokens to activate an equal number of experts within each predefined expert group. When a model execution is distributed on multiple devices, this architectural design ensures a balanced computational load across devices, significantly enhancing throughput, particularly for the inference phase. Further, we build Pangu Pro MoE on Ascend NPUs, a sparse model based on MoGE with 72 billion total parameters, 16 billion of which are activated for each token. The configuration of Pangu Pro MoE is optimized for Ascend 300I Duo and 800I A2 through extensive system simulation studies. Our experiments indicate that MoGE indeed leads to better expert load balancing and more efficient execution for both model training and inference on Ascend NPUs. The inference performance of Pangu Pro MoE achieves 1148 tokens/s per card and can be further improved to 1528 tokens/s per card by speculative acceleration, outperforming comparable 32B and 72B Dense models. Furthermore, we achieve an excellent cost-to-performance ratio for model inference on Ascend 300I Duo. Our studies show that Ascend NPUs are capable of training Pangu Pro MoE with massive parallelization to make it a leading model within the sub-100B total parameter class, outperforming prominent open-source models like GLM-Z1-32B and Qwen3-32B.

data.title: Mandelbrot in x86 Assembly by Claude
data.author: gslin
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者通过与AI助手Claude互动，尝试用x86汇编语言生成Mandelbrot分形图的过程。作者最初根据Claude生成的代码尝试在Mac上运行，但遇到编译问题。经过多轮调试和修改，包括使用Docker和调整汇编代码，最终成功生成了ASCII艺术形式的分形图。尽管最初结果不理想，全是"@"符号，但经过进一步调整，最终获得了满意的输出。文章还提供了完整的代码和Dockerfile，以及调试过程的记录。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在处理低级汇编代码和特定任务（如操作系统内核、Mandelbrot计算等）时的表现和实用性。

不同观点：
• noone_youknow：认为LLM在处理低级设备设置和引导代码（如汇编代码）时表现较差，经常生成无法正确汇编的代码，虚构硬件寄存器，且代码效率低下。然而，在将x86汇编代码移植到RISC-V时，LLM表现较好，因为这更像是一个简单的翻译任务。
• userbinator：指出LLM生成的代码有时存在明显错误，例如不必要的寄存器清零操作，这可能是因为训练数据中缺乏相关示例。
• abujazar：提到DeepSeek模型能一次性完成任务。
• pixelpoet：提醒大家注意Mandelbook和Claude Heiland-Allen在Mandelbrot方面的工作，以区分不同的技术贡献。
• sipsi：分享LLM生成3D星域代码的示例，虽然第一次尝试未使用正确的终端尺寸。
• horsellama：建议OP（原帖者）测试更具挑战性的代码高尔夫 Mandelbrot 汇编示例。
• broken_broken_：认为x64汇编代码可以在Mac上直接运行，无需Docker，只需调整系统调用号。如果使用ARM Mac，则可通过Rosetta运行。
• Jare：建议尝试在ARM汇编中使用LLM，因为训练集中可能较少有现成的代码。
• worldsayshi：对Claude Code的价格和实用性提出疑问，认为更多人应该使用Claude与aider和Copilot结合的方式。
• suddenlybananas：通过谷歌搜索发现大量Mandelbrot汇编示例，表明LLM可能参考了这些公开资源。
• piker：基于经验，预期LLM会继续遇到困难，但有时也能产生令人惊喜的结果。
• revskill：强烈批评LLM在实际代码库中的表现，认为其产生大量虚构和无意义的内容，且错误随机而不一致，只适合作为高级自动补全工具。
• ur-whale：对代码使用整数而非浮点数进行计算表示疑惑，询问原因。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个模型，如DeepSeek、Claude Code等，不同模型在特定任务上的表现引发对比和讨论。
• 对于Claude Code的价格和实用性存在争议，部分用户认为其性价比不高。
• 不同架构（x86、RISC-V、ARM）对LLM的表现影响显著，部分用户建议在较少训练数据的架构上进行测试。
• LLM生成代码的质量和可靠性是讨论的核心争议点，部分用户指出其虚构和错误问题严重。

44440509.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Mandelbrot in x86 assembly by Claude
. Inspired by
a tweet
asking if Claude knew x86 assembly, I decided to run a bit of an experiment.
I prompted Claude Sonnet 4:
Write me an ascii art mandelbrot fractal generator in x86 assembly
And
got back code
that looked... like assembly code I guess?
So I copied some jargon out of that response and asked:
I have some code written for x86-64 assembly using NASM syntax, targeting Linux (using system calls for output).
How can I run that on my Mac?
That
gave me a Dockerfile
.
I tried running it on my Mac and... it failed to compile.
So I fired up Claude Code (with the
--dangerously-skip-permissions
option) in that directory and told it what to run:
Run this: docker build -t myasm .
It started crunching. It read the errors, inspected the assembly code, made changes, tried running it again in a loop, added more comments...
...and eventually produced an ASCII art image of a fractal! Claude Code proudly declared:
Success! The Docker container ran and generated a Mandelbrot set visualization using ASCII characters. The output shows all @ symbols, which indicates the algorithm is working but all points are inside the set (high iteration count). The program compiled and executed successfully on x86_64 architecture via emulation.
Yeah... I was not satisfied with an image that was entirely @ symbols! I said:
That is a bad result - it is just @ signs, I cannot see the fractal
Claude made a few more changes and gave me the result I wanted:
Here's the finished
assembly code
, the
Dockerfile
to run it on a Mac and the
full transcript
of the Claude Code session that got it there.

data.title: Hexagon fuzz: Full-system emulated fuzzing of Qualcomm basebands
data.author: mschuster91
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种针对高通Hexagon基带处理器的全系统模拟模糊测试工具。由于Hexagon架构的专有性，目前缺乏相关的安全工具，导致其成为安全研究的盲点。研究团队开发了首个开源工具链，利用QEMU的Hexagon全系统模拟分支与LibAFL结合，实现了对Hexagon固件的模糊测试。该工具链显著减少了工程工作量，并支持覆盖率引导的模糊测试，填补了Hexagon基带安全研究的空白。通过该工具，研究人员可以对iPhone等设备中的Hexagon基带进行分析，解决了缺乏完整系统模拟和专用工具的问题。研究团队已在TROOPERS25会议上发布了这一工具链，并邀请社区共同协作改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Qualcomm基带处理器的安全性和零日漏洞的讨论，以及对该领域工具和市场竞争的分析。

不同观点：
• **le-mark**：对Qualcomm零日漏洞的潜在增加表示担忧，并质疑是否已有国家级攻击者利用了这些漏洞，而安全研究人员现在才开始追赶。
• **jasonjayr**：关注射频（RF）侧的模糊测试，提出软件定义无线电（SDR）揭示了许多开放的远程接口，这些接口的保护机制有限，仅依赖于“不应造成有害干扰”的原则。
• **xvilka**：提到Rizin工具对Hexagon指令集架构（ISA）和MDT镜像的支持，认为这有助于静态分析，并提供了相关实现的链接。
• **egberts1**：提供了Hexagon-based QEMU/Ghidra的.bin镜像资源链接，为有兴趣的开发者提供了具体参考。
• **mschuster91**：批评基带处理器市场的竞争环境，指出Qualcomm在市场上的主导地位导致代码质量和安全性投资不足。同时提到三星、华为和联发科的市场表现，并分析了进入该市场的难度。

补充讨论：
• **spr-alex**：简单表示了对文章的赞赏。
• **meerasmatkhan**：仅提到了“Tiktok”，与主要讨论点无直接关联。

争议焦点：
• Qualcomm在基带处理器市场的主导地位及其对安全性和代码质量的影响是争议的核心。mschuster91认为这种缺乏竞争的市场环境导致安全投资不足，而le-mark则隐含了对国家级攻击者可能早已利用这些漏洞的担忧。

44442189.article_content:
6/27/2025
Research by: Â
Bruno Produit, Luca Glockow, Rachna Shriwas
Hexagon fuzz: Full-system emulated fuzzing of Qualcomm basebands
Key takeaways
1. Due to Qualcommâs proprietary architecture, a lack of security tooling exists around their baseband
2. Our tooling enables research on Hexagon baseband with significantly reduced engineering work
3. We release the first open-source toolchain for full-system emulated Hexagon firmware fuzzing at
TROOPERS25
Overview
Every phone has a cellular baseband processor to handle mobile communications (5G, 4G, GPS, and more).
Qualcomm created a specific architecture for its baseband called Hexagon. It powers the baseband processors found in most leading smartphones, including every iPhone since generation 12 except iPhone 16e and all Snapdragon-based devices. This architecture, being different from the classic ARM, x86, or MIPS that we all know, leads to a lack of security research. Most of the produced tooling is simply not applicable to it!
We developed the first open-source toolchain for full-system emulated fuzzing of any Hexagon firmware. Our work addresses a gap in baseband security research by making a previously inaccessible attack surface available for analysis. With our toolchain, open-sourced
here
, we invite the community to collaborate and build upon this work.
Previous research landscape and the Hexagon gap
The baseband security research community has made considerable progress in recent years, yet a critical gap has persisted regarding Qualcommâs Hexagon architecture.
Early work like
BaseSAFE (2020, Maier and al.)
introduces an advanced framework for fuzzing basebands. Building on this,
FirmWire (2022, Hernandez et al.)
provides baseband emulation platforms for fuzzing.
These tools are the go-to solution for fuzzing basebands which use ARM, x86, MIPS and other standard architectures. But, as the FirmWire paper observes:
âUnlike other baseband implementations, Qualcomm leverages a fully-custom architecture known as Hexagon [â¦] Unfortunately, tooling for this architecture is sparse, and especially full-system emulators are lacking.â
Other research efforts around Hexagon are limited to specific aspects, such as DIAG protocol analysis and reverse engineering (see Figure 1).
Figure 1. Previous baseband research did not cover Hexagon baseband full system emulation
Challenges
Hexagon presents several barriers that make firmware analysis challenging:
Custom CPU architecture
: Most tooling lacks support, making reversing challenging
Custom OS and software stack
: Requires adapting common attack techniques
Custom communication protocols:
No free tools or documentation exist
The primary challenge in reversing Hexagon baseband lies in the lack of tooling support. Ghidra, IDA, and similar tools do not support the architecture out of the box, and while QEMU offers user-space emulation for Hexagon, full system emulation remains unavailable.
FirmWire, for example, relies on QEMU for emulation and introspection. Since Hexagon does not yet have proper full-system Hexagon emulation in QEMU, it is not possible to use it for analysing this firmware, as explained in the quote above.
Solution
To address these challenges, we used a QEMU fork from the Qualcomm Innovation Center (QuIC) supporting Hexagon full-system emulation. With the addition of LibAFLâs QEMU fork, we built a custom fuzzing and reverse engineering tool tailored for Hexagon.
â
1. How we merged QuIC/QEMU with LibAFLâs QEMU
The QEMU fork from QuIC includes a
hexagon_sysemu branch
that, with minor modifications, can successfully boot iPhone baseband firmware. We adapted this codebase for fuzzing by integrating it with
LibAFLâs QEMU
. Since the two projects share no common ancestor in Git, merging them requires significant manual effort and custom fixes.
We share our QEMU fork in
this
repository, which can be used directly. Like QuICâs fork, you can emulate Hexagon firmware and connect LLDB if you have Qualcommâs Hexagon SDK. You can also compile it as a library and connect LibAFL for introspection directly in Rust via its elegant API.
2. How we created a fully coverage-guided fuzzer
Using this approach, we can recreate something similar to FirmWire and use Rust-based hooks for control flow modification. When booting a baseband firmware, these code flow manipulations are necessary. The emulator wonât provide the hardware components that the firmware communicates with.
We created a fuzzer that handles control flow manipulation for a specific iPhone firmware, up to user mode, utilizing these LibAFL bindings. We provide this with a JSON-based approach, where you can set breakpoints with their handlers in the configuration. You can also modify the QEMU command line arguments to debug firmware emulation issues.
Figure 2. Snippet of the JSON-based configuration for Hexagon fuzz
With this tooling, a fully coverage-guided fuzzer can run on any Hexagon-based baseband firmware. This way, all the 5G/4G/GP

data.title: A proof-of-concept neural brain implant providing speech
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了加州大学戴维斯分校的科学家团队研发的一种新型神经假体，能够将脑信号直接转化为声音，实现实时语音交流。与以往将脑信号转化为文本的系统不同，该系统可以捕捉语音的细微差别，如音高和韵律，并以低延迟生成语音。过去此类系统存在延迟高、词汇有限以及无法处理非预设语言或名称等问题。团队通过256个微电极记录脑信号，并使用神经解码器和声码器合成语音。参与研究的ALS患者T15通过该系统实现了更自然流畅的交流。这项技术标志着向全数字化发声系统迈出了重要一步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：脑机接口设备的技术挑战、实际应用和未来潜力

不同观点：
• [x187463] 关注设备触发声音产生的机制，担心设备可能会无意中表达出用户不想公开的思维。这涉及到设备的激活机制以及与神经元的连接方式，用户对设备的控制程度是其主要关切点。

• [yaris] 对设备研发过程中所需的技术和设备来源感到好奇，质疑这些设备是外购还是内部自制，反映了公众对高科技设备研发过程的不了解以及对技术供应链的兴趣。

• [N_Lens] 认为神经-计算机接口，特别是电极技术，是当前发展的主要瓶颈。提出通过增加电极数量来突破瓶颈的常见方法，但也设想了非传统方法（如高保真合成神经纤维）作为潜在解决方案，显示出对技术创新的开放态度。

• [andrybak] 对研究成果的标题和宣传持批评态度，认为标题有误导性（点击诱饵），因为当前技术还不能实现清晰可懂的实时对话，强调目前只是概念验证阶段，而非成熟应用。

• [pingou] 展望了脑机接口技术的未来应用，包括“心灵感应”式的直接脑对脑通信，但也认识到信号转换和翻译的必要性，表现出对技术未来发展的乐观态度。

Stephen Hawking, a British physicist and arguably the most famous man suffering from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), communicated with the world using a sensor installed in his glasses. That sensor used tiny movements of a single muscle in his cheek to select characters on a screen. Once he typed a full sentence at a rate of roughly one word per minute, the text was synthesized into speech by a DECtalk TC01 synthesizer, which gave him his iconic, robotic voice.
But a lot has changed since Hawking died in 2018. Recent brain-computer-interface (BCI) devices have made it possible to translate neural activity directly into text and even speech. Unfortunately, these systems had significant latency, often limiting the user to a predefined vocabulary, and they did not handle nuances of spoken language like pitch or prosody. Now, a team of scientists at the University of California, Davis has built a neural prosthesis that can instantly translate brain signals into sounds—phonemes and words. It may be the first real step we have taken toward a fully digital vocal tract.
Text messaging
“Our main goal is creating a flexible speech neuroprosthesis that enables a patient with paralysis to speak as fluently as possible, managing their own cadence, and be more expressive by letting them modulate their intonation,” says Maitreyee Wairagkar, a neuroprosthetics researcher at UC Davis who led the study. Developing a prosthesis ticking all these boxes was an enormous challenge because it meant Wairagkar’s team had to solve nearly all the problems BCI-based communication solutions have faced in the past. And they had quite a lot of problems.
The first issue was moving beyond text—most successful neural prostheses developed so far have translated brain signals into text—the words a patient with an implanted prosthesis wanted to say simply appeared on a screen. Francis R. Willett led a team at Stanford University that
achieved
brain-to-text translation with around a 25 percent error rate. “When a woman with ALS was trying to speak, they could decode the words. Three out of four words were correct. That was super exciting but not enough for daily communication,” says Sergey Stavisky, a neuroscientist at UC Davis and a senior author of the study.
Delays and dictionaries
One year after the Stanford work, in 2024, Stavisky’s team
published
its own research on a brain-to-text system that bumped the accuracy to 97.5 percent. “Almost every word was correct, but communicating over text can be limiting, right?” Stavisky said. “Sometimes you want to use your voice. It allows you to make interjections, it makes it less likely other people interrupt you—you can sing, you can use words that aren’t in the dictionary.” But the most common approach to generating speech relied on synthesizing it from text, which led straight into another problem with BCI systems: very high latency.
In nearly all BCI speech aids, sentences appeared on a screen after a significant delay, long after the patient finished stringing the words together in their mind. The speech synthesis part usually happened after the text was ready, which caused even more delay. The latest system of this kind supported a dictionary of 125,000 words but it still failed when you tried to speak a different language or even say the unusual name of a café just around the corner.
So, Wairagkar designed her prosthesis to translate brain signals into sounds, not words—and do it in real time.
Extracting sound
The patient who agreed to participate in Wairagkar’s study was codenamed T15 and was a 46-year-old man suffering from ALS. “He is severely paralyzed and when he tries to speak, he is very difficult to understand. I’ve known him for several years, and when he speaks, I understand maybe 5 percent of what he’s saying,” says David M. Brandman, a neurosurgeon and co-author of the study. Before working with the UC Davis team, T15 communicated using a gyroscopic head mouse to control a cursor on a computer screen.
To use an early version of Stavisky’s brain-to-text system, the patient had 256 microelectrodes implanted into his ventral precentral gyrus, an area of the brain responsible for controlling vocal tract muscles.
For the new brain-to-speech system, Wairagkar and her colleagues relied on the same 256 electrodes. “We recorded neural activities from single neurons, which is the highest resolution of information we can get from our brain,” Wairagkar says. The signal registered by the electrodes was then sent to an AI algorithm called a neural decoder that deciphered those signals and extracted speech features such as pitch or voicing. In the next step, these features were fed into a vocoder, a speech synthesizing algorithm designed to sound like the voice that T15 had when he was still able to speak normally. data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要回顾了大型语言模型（LLM）的基础模型发展趋势，重点介绍模型大小和训练数据，不包含谣言或未证实的信息。文章提到：

1. **GPT-2系列（2019）**：包括1.37亿到16.1亿参数，训练数据集为WebText，约100亿token。
2. **GPT-3（2020）**：1,750亿参数，训练数据包括CommonCrawl、WebText2、Books1、Books2和Wikipedia，约4,000亿token，训练耗时数月，使用大量GPU。
3. **GPT-3.5和GPT-4（2022-2023）**：无官方架构或训练数据信息。
4. **Llama系列**：包括70亿到650亿参数，其中Llama 65B训练了1.4万亿token。Llama 405B（2024）模型通过高质量数据提升性能，但出现偏离纯文本生成引擎的趋势。
5. **Llama-4（2025）**：包含2万亿参数的MoE模型，但因学术不当行为引发信任危机，未正式发布。
6. **早期模型匮乏**：长时间没有与GPT-3相当的模型，直到405B模型发布成为转折点。

文章还指出，模型训练逐渐偏向优化基准性能，而非纯粹的文本生成。

base model trends.md
How large are large language models? (2025)
This aims to be factual information about the size of large language models. None of this document was written by AI. I do not include any information from leaks or rumors. The focus of this document is on base models (the raw text continuation engines, not 'helpful chatbot/assistants'). This is a view from a few years ago to today of one very tiny fraction of the larger LLM story that's happening.
History
GPT-2,-medium,-large,-xl
(2019): 137M, 380M, 812M, 1.61B. Source:
openai-community/gpt2
. Trained on the unreleased
WebText
dataset said to 40GB of Internet text - I estimate that to be roughly 10B tokens. You can see a list of the websites that went into that data set here
domains.txt
.
GPT-3 aka davinci, davinci-002
(2020): 175B parameters. There is a good breakdown of how those parameters are 'spent' here
How does GPT-3 spend its 175B parameters?
. Trained on around 400B tokens composed of CommonCrawl, WebText2, Books1, Books2 and Wikipedia. Source
Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
. These training runs required months of a data center full of tens of thousands of A100 GPUs
source
.
GPT-3.5, GPT-4
(2022, 2023): No official factual information on architecture or training data available.
Llama
*
Llama 7B, 13B, 33B, 65B
: The 65B model was pretrained on a 1.4T (trillion tokens) dataset. LLaMA was officially stated to use Books3
source
as a data set - this is a very important dataset which has been pivotal in lawmaking regarding the training of AIs on large amounts of copyrighted and potentially pirated material.
Llama-3.1 405B
(2024): The 405B llama model was released. This is a dense transformer model, meaning all parameters are used in inference passes. Initial pretraining: 2.87T tokens, long context: 800B, annealing: 40M - so 3.67T total. source:
The Llama 3 Herd of Models
. By this point meta has learned to say less about what data goes into the models
"We create our dataset for language model pre-training from a variety of data sources containing knowledge"
- so I can't say as much about what goes into the training data here.
Empirically, we find that annealing (see Section 3.4.3) on small amounts of high-quality code and mathematical data can boost the performance of pre-trained models on key benchmarks
The emerging trend of
annealing
pretrained models to 'benchmax' is unfortunate in that it biases the base language models somewhat away from being pure text continuation engines. This should really be part of the post-training which aims to make the models role play as some kind of AI-chatbot helpful assistant character. But these companies care very much about metrics and scores.
Llama-4
(2025): The largest in the llama4 family is a 2T total parameter MoE model - A288B 16E (active 288B parameters, 16 Experts).
It is unreleased
. As for the smaller llama4 models (which are distilled from the large one): There was a scandal as facebook decided to mislead people by gaming the lmarena benchmark site - they served one version of llama4 maverick there and released a different version of llama4 maverick, for some reason. This academic misconduct led to reduced trust in the llama team which seems to have imploded shortly after. It's unclear if the 2T Behemoth model will ever be released after what happened. The smaller LLama4 models (maverick and scout), are distilled off this large one, and are generally considered to be of low-intelligence.
The desert
For a long time, there weren't really any
large
language models available to download. There was certainly nothing comparable with GPT-3 for a few years. There were projects to try to match it, but generally they operated by fine tuning things like small (70B) llama models on a bunch of GPT-3 generated texts (synthetic data - which can result in degeneration when AI outputs are fed back into AI training intputs).

主要讨论点：如何将SaaS产品销售给中小企业和大型企业，以及在销售过程中遇到的挑战和策略。

不同观点：
• **Mekoka的观点**：认为向大型企业销售SaaS时，需要针对有决策权的人，并提出不仅要销售工具，还要提供解决问题的服务，成为“魔术师”来吸引客户注意。
• **Bitbasher的观点**：强调时机和精准营销，建议通过社交媒体监控客户的痛点，并通过提供付费产品试用而不是“免费试用”来吸引客户。同时，强调快速响应和从取消订阅的客户那里获取反馈的重要性。
• **Jwr的观点**：指出市场营销变得更为重要和困难，传统广告效果不佳，内容营销也因SEO和AI生成内容的泛滥而变得更具挑战性。
• **Codingdave的观点**：认为客户只关心“更多价值”如果它能解决更多问题，建议通过与客户沟通来了解他们的痛点并调整产品价值主张。
• **Pradeepodela的观点**：分享了自己在产品推广中遇到的流量和目标用户不匹配的问题，并指出即使产品好，如果没有足够的曝光也难以成功。
• **Vlod的观点**：质疑产品是否经过客户验证，建议首先要确保产品对客户当前的工作流程有明显改善，否则即使产品再好也难以销售。
• **Jameslk的观点**：区分了自上而下和自下而上的销售策略，指出针对不同层次的客户需要不同的销售和营销方法，强调关系和早期验证的重要性。
• **Bko的观点**：认为直接销售是唯一有效的方法，建议通过与客户直接沟通来了解他们的问题，而不是直接推销产品。
• **Kjksf的观点**：指出提供具体的网站和营销材料对于给出具体建议至关重要，强调细节决定成败。
• **Wiradikusuma的观点**：分享了自己通过个人关系获得付费客户的经验，并对教科书式的数字营销效果表示怀疑。
• **Throwawayffffas的观点**：建议通过现实世界中的会面来展示产品，并认为面对面的交流能获得更真实的反馈。
• **Jpc0的观点**：认为如果连自己都不相信产品，那就无法成功销售，强调自信心的重要性。
• **Franze的观点**：简单直接地问是否已经有一个付费客户，暗示获取第一个付费客户是关键步骤。
• **Sakerbos的观点**：强调利用自己的人脉网络，认为通过口碑可以获得更多的付费客户。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：如何有效销售SaaS产品，特别是在大型企业和中小企业的不同策略上，以及数字营销与个人关系在销售中的相对重要性。
• **重要论据和例子**：
  - Mekoka提到提供服务以解决客户问题。
  - Bitbasher分享了通过社交媒体监控和快速响应获得客户的经验。
  - Jwr指出传统广告和内容营销的困难。
  - Pradeepodela强调流量和目标用户匹配的重要性。
  - Vlod质疑产品是否经过客户验证。
  - Jameslk详细描述了自上而下和自下而上的销售策略。
  - Bko强调直接销售和与客户沟通的重要性。
  - Kjksf指出具体细节对给出建议的重要性。
  - Wiradikusuma通过个人关系获得付费客户的经验。
  - Throwawayffffas建议通过面对面的会面获得反馈。
  - Jpc0强调自信心对销售成功的重要性。
  - Franze和sakerbos都认为获得第一个付费客户是关键。

这些观点和例子为销售SaaS产品提供了多种策略和思考角度，特别是针对不同类型客户和市场环境的适应性。

data.author: julianh65
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者对收集到的数千个益智药（nootropics）评分的分析。益智药广义上指任何声称能提升认知能力的物质，包括处方药、植物、少量娱乐药物以及像睡眠和锻炼等活动。由于个体差异，益智药的效果因人而异。作者开发了一个推荐系统，用户输入自己尝试过的益智药评分，系统会推荐可能适合他们的其他益智药。作者收集了1981人的29,387个评分，加上之前的数据共36,163个评分。评分采用0-10的尺度，0代表完全无效或副作用过大，1-4代表可能有效果，5-9代表明显效果，10代表改变生活。分析中考虑了缺乏随机分配、自我报告偏差和缺乏控制与盲法等偏见。这些评分帮助预测某个人对特定益智药的潜在反应，但需注意结果可能受到 placebo 效应的影响。所有数据和代码均公开。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：有关益智药（nootropics）的有效性和安全性讨论

不同观点：
• **益智药与自然活动的对比**：
   - **negativepanda**：认为简单的益智药如咖啡加上自然散步比单独做一件事效果更好，且这种组合能带来期待感。
   - **reverendsteveii**：通过每天20分钟的阻力训练和有氧运动，得到了显著的益智效果，并认为运动是改变生活的“益智药”。

• **益智药效果的持久性与副作用**：
   - **icameron**：基于个人经验，认为益智药在初期效果明显，但随着时间推移，大脑会适应，效果减弱，甚至可能产生副作用，最终适得其反。例如SNRIs和Kratom都出现了类似的问题。
   - **butlike**：指出像安非他明这样的药物可能带来的改变未必是正面的，暗指其潜在的负面影响。

• **对益智药讨论的信任问题**：
   - **taeric**：认为由于缺乏大规模随机试验，益智药的讨论充满不确定性，尤其在自己使用Adderall的情况下，更加难以信任这些讨论。
   - **cckolon**：质疑个人经验的说服力，认为如果没有盲法试验，很难确定效果是否为安慰剂效应。

• **特定物质的讨论**：
   - **gavinray**：认为Modafinil、Racetams、Phenibut等物质效果明显，但Noopept未被提及，表示困惑。
   - **wslh**：强调某些物质如安非他明对大脑功能有直接且不可逆的影响，需给予强烈警告，与Omega-3等其他物质形成对比。

• **运动作为益智药的讨论**：
   - **Workaccount2**：强调运动的重要性，批评许多人抱怨健康问题却不愿尝试运动。
   - **Analemma_**：总结认为，除ADHD药物外，大多数益智药效果有限，而运动尤其是重量训练和高强度间歇训练（HIIT）具有显著益智效果，这符合进化视角。

补充讨论：
• **益智药的文化与信息来源**：
   - **readthenotes1**：提到益智药社区和初学者指南，并指出一些信息中的拼写错误，反映出对益智药讨论中的信息质量问题。

• **外部资源与数据支持**：
   - **runamuck**：提到Scott Alexander的益智药调查和分析，提供了一个外部资源以供参考。

争议焦点：
• 益智药的长期效果与副作用：个人经验显示益智药初期有效，但随着时间推移效果减弱并可能产生副作用，这与运动等自然方式的持久效果形成对比。
• 对益智药讨论的信任度：缺乏大规模试验导致对益智药效果的信任问题，尤其是在涉及药物如Adderall的情况下。

总结：评论围绕益智药的有效性、副作用、自然活动的替代效果以及对益智药讨论的信任问题展开，强调了运动作为一种有效的益智方式，并对某些药物的长期效果和潜在风险提出了警告。

Home

What I learned gathering thousands of nootropic ratings
March 23, 2022
tags:
nootropics
,
data-analysis
Credit: Ultra Heaven
In this post, I analyze nootropics ratings I gathered through a
recommender system
. Jump directly to
What I learned
if you don’t like caveats and methodology.
INTRODUCTION
#
What is a nootropic?
I will use the term
nootropic
as broadly as possible to describe
“Any substance purported to increase or enhance cognitive abilities."
Some only use the term
nootropic
to refer to a specific thing which should check a
very specific checklist
, e.g. having very few side-effects. As I’m not using this definition,
remember that the
nootropics
mentioned here can be very dangerous
.
This includes prescribed medications, plants, recreational drugs in small quantities, and more (I even included activities like sleep or exercise). If you hadn’t heard of “nootropics” before, you should also know that some people like to experiment with them and share their experience on communities like the
nootropics subreddit
, which has a great
begginer’s guide
.
The effectiveness of a nootropic varies a lot from one person to another (
your mileage will vary
). This is why I built a
nootropic recommendation system
Enter ratings on nootropics you’ve tried, and it will spit out nootropics liked by people with similar rating patterns. This was initially based on the
2016 SlateStarCodex nootropics survey
data.
, which I suggest you try before reading this post.
Still, it is helpful to understand how good each nootropic is in general, if only to prioritize further research. Indeed, my cunning plan with this recommendation system was to incentivize people to answer a boring survey. My plan worked better than I expected, and I got 1981 people to enter 29,387 nootropic ratings
Adding to it the original SlateStarCodex data, we have 36,163 ratings from 2,802 people.
, which I analyse in this post. Thanks everybody!
All data and code can be found
here
.
RATINGS
#
People interested in the code or the details of the analysis can look at
the RMarkdown notebook
.
How to interpret these ratings
#
Scale
#
I used the scale from
SlateStarCodex nootropics surveys
, which is:
0 means a substance was totally useless, or had so many side effects you couldn’t continue taking it.
1 - 4 means subtle effects, maybe placebo but still useful.
5 - 9 means strong effects, definitely not placebo.
10 means life-changing.
Ok but why?
I mostly used this scale so I could use SSC data when launching my recommendation system, but let me try to defend it. When someone tries a nootropic, either it seems to work, and the person will continue taking it, or it doesn’t seem to work, and the person will quickly stop taking it. This means we should expect people to have more certainty about nootropics that seem to work at least a little than on nootropics that don’t seem to work. If we want to compress a user experience into a 1D number, it makes sense to allow a more fine-grained judgment on positive nootropics
Why not make a scale from -10 to 10 then? Well, I just stole the scale, you know, but I think people really hate entering fine-grained ratings when they don’t have enough information.
. An issue is that this doesn’t differentiate between “Doesn’t do anything” and “I cannot feel my left arm anymore after trying this nootropic”. I tried to remedy this by asking people about the issues they had. Another issue is that some people might not read the scale description and think below 5 is negative and above is positive. I tried to take this into account in my analysis.
Biases
#
In order of importance (I think):
Lack of random allocation
The people who entered their rating on my recommender system were not randomly assigned to try specific nootropics. Thus we can expect a (usually positive) correlation between “I’m likely to try nootropic A” and “Nootropic A might work on me”.
This means that my estimations don’t represent the ratings a random person would get on average (which would usually be lower); they’re instead a prediction of the rating that a person would give to a nootropic if they decided to take it organically. Take this into account when transferring the results to yourself.
Self-report
You take a pill. It makes you feel good. You go on a website which asks you how good the pill is. You say it’s awesome. Little did you know that it was, in fact, merely good.
Take this into account when reading these ratings, especially if improving your mood is not your main goal.
Lack of control and blinding
Relatedly, these uncontrolled and unblinded ratings are partly driven by the placebo effect.
The sophisticated objection would be that this is probably less of a problem than for normal medications. The
placebo effect seems to be in large part due to regression to the mean
(when you’re sick, you’ll likely get better with time, not worse), which should not be an issue for nootropics in most cases. But the placebo effect does seem to be r

总结：评论围绕益智药的有效性、副作用、自然活动的替代效果以及对益智药讨论的信任问题展开，强调了运动作为一种有效的益智方式，并对某些药物的长期效果和潜在风险提出了警告。

data.title: I'm dialing back my LLM usage
data.author: sagacity
data.article_summary:
Alberto Fortin是一位有15年经验的软件工程师，他分享了使用大型语言模型（LLM）的实际体验。最初，他对LLM充满热情，希望其能革新开发流程，但在使用Go和ClickHouse重建基础设施时遇到许多问题。他的博客和后续分析指出，AI的宣传与现实存在差距，尽管新模型如Claude Opus 4有所改进，但仍未完全解决核心问题。

Alberto强调，LLM在初期使用时看似能大幅提升生产力，但实际上在处理复杂生产代码时经常出现错误，导致开发者需要耗费更多时间修复。他建议开发者应将LLM视为辅助工具，而非主导，保持对代码库的完全掌控。最终，他呼吁理性看待AI技术，既要利用其优势，也要认识到其局限性，找到平衡的使用方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）在编程中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **LLMs在生成代码方面的局限性**：[x187463] 认为LLMs生成的代码缺乏开发者的认知参与，管理这些代码很困难，尤其在需要长期维护的项目中。LLMs更适合一次性脚本或短期项目。
• **LLMs可能降低生产力**：[stephendause] 指出LLMs有时会因为提供错误信息而让用户走上错误的路径，浪费时间。虽然总体上LLMs是有帮助的，但需要用户检查其来源。
• **LLMs如类固醇，效果与副作用并存**：[noisy_boy] 将LLMs比作类固醇，认为其能快速提高生产力，但副作用明显，例如编程能力的退化。
• **LLMs忽视简单而重要的设计原则**：[jimbokun] 认为LLMs容易生成复杂的、难以重构和理解的代码，而忽视了将复杂问题分解为简单组件的重要性。
• **LLMs作为代码审查和概念解释工具**：[seanw444] 和[Const-me] 都将LLMs用作个性化的、快速的知识获取工具，而不是完整的代码生成器。Const-me还提到LLMs在代码审查中的作用，尽管需要筛选其建议。

补充讨论：
• **LLMs的局限性和特定领域表现不佳**：[quaintdev] 分享了LLMs在解决特定技术问题时的不足，例如无法提供最佳解决方案。
• **LLMs是新的速成方案现象**：[andy99] 认为LLMs是一种新的快速解决方案潮流，但现实中并没有真正的捷径，只有权衡和取舍。
• **LLMs在不同工作流中的应用**：[jjice] 和[hedgehog] 都提到LLMs在减少重复性工作方面的优势，例如生成模板代码和测试。同时，他们也强调了提示词优化和代码审查的重要性。
• **LLMs信仰与实际效果的争议**：[obirunda] 指出了对LLMs效果的信仰差异，一些人认为LLMs能大幅提高生产力，而另一些人则对其效果持怀疑态度。
• **LLMs未来发展的可能性**：[kadhirvelm] 提出了LLMs作为编译器的未来可能性，认为未来可能无需直接关注代码，而只需关注功能特性。

争议焦点：
• LLMs在编程中的实际效果和长期影响：一些人认为LLMs能显著提高生产力，而另一些人则担心其副作用和对开发者能力的侵蚀。
• LLMs在生成和维护复杂代码项目中的可行性：有观点认为LLMs更适合一次性任务或简单任务，而在复杂项目中表现不佳。

44443109.article_content:
← Back to Blog
Why I'm Dialing Back My LLM Usage
Alberto Fortin
From the
Agentic Engineering Sessions
|
Aired on
July 1st, 2025
We invited
Alberto Fortin
, a seasoned software engineer with 15 years of experience, to share his candid journey with AI. Alberto initially embraced LLMs with genuine enthusiasm, hoping they would revolutionize his development workflow. However, after encountering significant challenges while rebuilding his infrastructure with Go and ClickHouse, he wrote a
thoughtful blog post
reflecting on the gap between AI hype and reality.
For this conversation, Alberto also prepared a
detailed follow-up analysis
testing newer models like Claude Opus 4, examining whether recent improvements have addressed the core issues he encountered.
His experience provides practical lessons for engineers evaluating LLMs in production environments—balancing realistic expectations with an understanding of where these tools genuinely add value versus where they still fall short.
You can
watch the session on YouTube
or read below for some selected quotes.
The Reality Check: When AI Hype Meets Production Code
"I was really shocked at the poor quality of some things, and it was not just about bugs and features not working. I think as a developer who wants to maintain this codebase for the next few years, I also care about it being neat enough."
"I feel like I'm a week away from fixing this, but actually a new small error would come up and then that will take another two weeks to fix."
"I will give my error output to the LLM and then it will spit out something new that will kind of fix it, but also make things a bit more messed up—and break something else in the process."
The Productivity Illusion
"I think everyone just got a little bit overexcited about it because the first iteration, the first little feature, the first autocomplete is like, 'Oh my God, this is amazing. This is like reading my mind.' So you kind of get duped into it a little bit."
"I think we've gotten to a level where we can do probably 10 times as much coding. So we kind of expect that to happen and we require that from the LLMs, but I think everyone just gets a little bit overexcited about it."
Taking Control: The Mental Shift
"I think this is the biggest difference, like a mental shift... I am the software engineer, the senior software engineer, I am the architect. The LLM is the assistant. The assistant responds to me; I make the plan."
"I lost all my trust in LLMs, so I wouldn't give them a big feature again. I'll do very small things like refactoring or a very small-scoped feature."
"I started fixing the bugs myself. Because as soon as you understand this—you have a hundred percent understanding of your codebase and what everything is doing—it's so much easier and quicker for you to go in and fix something."
Practical Wisdom
"If you are confident enough in your skills—you know, a senior developer—and this is not working for you, there's nothing wrong with you. Just try to do the things that you always did and use AI to leverage your knowledge a little bit."
"We've gone up a level, it's great. But also, let's be mindful we're not there yet at the next level... We are offloading some of the programming work, but we still need to do architectural abstractions and make the decisions for the product."
"Let's just try to calm down all this hype and find a balanced approach towards AI. Use it, because I think it's such an amazing revolution in technology, but we're not there yet."
Learn more about Agentic Engineering
Working toward genuine, quality software in an era where code production is not the constraint anymore. Learn our take about
Agentic Engineering
and catch up with all the sessions where we're joined by experts to further develop this topic.

data.title: Exploiting the IKKO Activebuds "AI powered" earbuds
data.author: ajdude
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者购买并研究一款运行Android系统的无线耳塞式设备的过程。该设备因其集成了ChatGPT和其他AI功能而在TikTok上走红。作者通过ADB方式破解设备，发现其直接与OpenAI的API通信，并包含一个OpenAI的密钥。设备还提供了一些应用程序，如Spotify和游戏，但由于屏幕小，操作不便。在研究过程中，作者提取了设备中的APK文件，发现了加密的API端点和密钥，并成功在一个已root的设备上运行了相关应用。此外，作者还提到设备有不同的模式，如“愤怒的Dan”和“恋爱中的Dan”，这些模式有不同的系统提示。最终，作者对该设备的安全性和功能实现提出了质疑和分析。

44443919.article_content:
So my journey with these earbuds started after I saw them on
this
Mrwhosetheboss video about pointless tech. This device seems to be also popular on TikTok. My suspicions were confirmed, this runs android. So of course i went ahead and bought them.
245 euros later... and they finally arrived!
Before we dive further into this, unlike with
rabbit
, this issue has been properly reported and patched. This is also my first real blog post/disclosure so feedback is appreciated.
Small overview
I like how they strapped a USB-c cable to the outside of the box while there is also a smaller one inside the box. They ran out of box space it seems...
I also wonder if they are legally allowed to use this OpenAI logo (probably not lol)
Anyways, we aren't here for fancy boxes, lets get to the main point. The device itself boots up to a screen with the time and ChatGPT front and center.
There are some other AI features available too like translations. But this isn't a review of the device, you can watch
other YouTube videos
about that. The ChatGPT animation looks way too similar to the actual app and OpenAI could probably get them in legal trouble for stealing their brand identity. I will also mention that the audio quality is absolute shit if you use their EQ profiles but can be upped to a usable level by tweaking the EQ curves yourself.
There are also some apps available in the IKKO store, the reason that there is no google play store available is because these apps are modified specifically for the screen on the ActiveBuds, at least, that is what the CEO says about them. We will check that out in a bit. These apps include some music apps like Spotify, but also some gaming apps like, oh god, SUBWAY SURFERS BAYBEEEEE
Of course all of them unbearable to navigate due to the small screen. However we can now confirm that it most definitely runs android.
Time for some hacking
There is sadly no browser available to directly download other apps. And while you can open the native android settings app, clicking the build number 7 times does not enable developer mode. So i couldn't enable adb it seems. Is it locked that well? heh nope.
Let's just plug it into a pc and see what happens....
What the fuck, they left ADB enabled. Well, this makes it a lot easier.
After sideloading the obligatory DOOM, i began checking out how the ChatGPT integration works on the backend. I first started HTTP inspecting the device, however since i couldn't enable the proper system certificates without rooting the device, i couldn't see exactly to what URL it communicated. Fortunately that wasn't really needed.
Holy shit, holy shit, holy shit, it communicates DIRECTLY TO OPENAI. This means that a ChatGPT key must be present on the device!
I know that this device can be rooted to get the proper certificates installed because
a tool
exists on all Spreadtrum/Unisoc devices which can be used to unlock the bootloader as long as companies use the default signing keys. This was indeed the case here too. However, i couldn't get past the confirmation screen as the device does not have a volume up key to confirm the unlock. I think you are able to sign your own partitions to make it flash them without an unlocked bootloader but that's a bit too advanced for my own liking.
So, i went back to the drawing board and just dumped all of the apps from it with an APK extractor tool. After popping the launcher app into JADX, things immediately became concerning.
The device can communicate to either of these domains.
api.openai.com
Obvious, the OpenAI API
chat1.chat.iamjoy.cn
Seems to be the API for the entire device, including features not related to ChatGPT like the app store. Loading it up in a browser gives a login page.
chat2.chat.iamjoy.cn
Same thing as chat1, possibly a backup server?
openspeech.bytedance.com
No idea, might be a speech recogniser backup instead of whisper, haven't seen communication to this from the device.
www.airdimple.cn
Seems like an OpenAI API mirror or proxy?
Knowing this i went hunting for api endpoints and keys. I found a file called SecurityStringsAPI which contained encrypted endpoints and authentication keys.
You might think, hey that's just base64 idiot, the most basic encoding known to mankind. And well, yeah, it is.
However, there is a second stage which is handled by a native library which is obfuscated to hell. I am not going to even try to read that. Fortunately i didn't have to. I just sideloaded the app on a different device which was rooted, and well,
just like the rabbit apk
, it just works!
Inspecting this device:
Yup, that's an OpenAI key.
Now, while having this access, we can also expose their (pretty funny) system prompt.
The device also has another few modes, which are Angry Dan and In-Love Dan. For the angry one you need to confirm you are 18+ because it actually swears a lot.
The system prompts for these are a bit more boring.
I also noticed that it logs the chat to another endpoint on the chat1 domain. This is probably just

data.title: Azure API vulnerability and roles misconfiguration compromise corporate networks
data.author: ArielSimon
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Azure角色权限过度授予和API漏洞带来的安全风险。安全研究人员发现，一些Azure内置角色被错误配置为权限过度宽泛，授予了超出预期的权限。此外，Azure API存在一个漏洞，可能导致VPN密钥泄露。这两者结合形成了一条新的攻击链，使低权限用户能够访问内部云资源和本地网络。

文章首先介绍了Azure RBAC（基于角色的访问控制）的基本概念，包括安全主体、角色定义和权限范围。Azure提供超过400个内置角色，分为通用角色和服务特定角色。通用角色易于管理但权限较宽，而服务特定角色更安全但需要更细致的管理。

研究揭示了一些角色如“Reader”和“Workbook Reader”的权限定义相对合理，但“Managed Applications Reader”等角色可能被不当利用，导致潜在安全风险。

为防范这些威胁，组织应仔细审查角色权限分配，采用最小权限原则，并及时更新安全策略。

Azure's Role Roulette: How Over-Privileged Roles and API Vulnerabilities Expose Enterprise Networks
Ariel Simon
Security Researcher
No items found.
TL;DR
Token Security researchers have discovered several Azure built-in roles that are misconfigured to be over-privileged - they grant more permissions than intended by Azure.
In addition, we discovered another vulnerability in the Azure API that allows attackers to
leak VPN keys
.
Combined, these two issues create a new attack chain that lets a
weak user gain access to both internal cloud assets and on-premises networks.
In this report, we detail the research process that led to the discoveries, their implications, and what organizations can do to stay safe against these threats and other identity-driven attacks.
What is Azure RBAC?
Before jumping in, letâs discuss some basics.
Azureâs permissions model, Azure RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), is, as the name states, based on roles.
Roles are basically groups of permissions that can be assigned to principals (users, service principals, groups, etc). When granting a role to a principal, you create a
role assignment
.
â
Every
role assignment
contains three main components:
Security Principal
- Who is given the permissions?
Role Definition
- Which role is assigned? What permissions does it grant? This section states the name of the role and the
Actions
and
Not Actions
(allow or deny) that this role is granting.
Scope
- What resources is the principal given access to? The scope can be vast, such as an entire management group or subscription, or more specific, like a resource group or a single resource (e.g., a specific VM or storage account).
Role assignment
Azure roles
In Azure, there are more than 400 built-in roles, which can be divided into 2 categories:
Generic
- Roles that grant permissions that apply across all resources and all Azure services in the given scope (e.g.,
Contributor
,
Owner
,
Reader
,
etc.
)
Service-specific
- Roles that grant permissions for a specific service or function in the given scope (e.g.,
Storage Blob Data Reader
or
Virtual Machine Contributor
).
If you assign the
Contributor
role over a subscription scope, it will grant permissions to perform actions over all of the resources in this subscription, regardless if theyâre storage accounts, virtual machines, or any other resource. But if you assign the
Virtual Machine Contributor
, it will grant these permissions only to perform actions over virtual machines in the subscription.
So we can see the tradeoff here: using service-specific roles is the more secure approach, since you are granting fewer permissions, but the generic roles are easier to use since you need to manage fewer roles assignments.
The Problem
Letâs take a look at few roles and their permissions. See if you can tell where things go wrong.
The Reader role
One of Azureâs built-in roles, called
Reader,
is a generic role. As youâd expect, it gives read-only permissions over the resources in the chosen scope. Letâs examine its
role definition
:
{
"assignableScopes": [
"/"
],
"description": "View all resources, but does not allow you to make any changes.",
"id": "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7",
"name": "acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7",
"permissions": [
{
"actions": [
"*/read"
],
"notActions": [],
"dataActions": [],
"notDataActions": []
}
],
"roleName": "Reader",
"roleType": "BuiltInRole",
"type": "Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions"
}
Reader role definition
As we can see in the
actions
property, the permission given is
*/read
, which means it lets you perform any read action in the given scope.
*Note that this does not include data actions (reading data objects like files in storage accounts, key vault secrets, etc). Those require different, service-specific sensitive permissions.
Okay, so a generic role giving generic read permissions, that makes sense.
What about the permissions of service-specific roles?
Workbook Reader
{
"assignableScopes": [
"/"
],
"description": "Can read workbooks.",
"id": "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/b279062a-9be3-42a0-92ae-8b3cf002ec4d",
"name": "b279062a-9be3-42a0-92ae-8b3cf002ec4d",
"permissions": [
{
"actions": [
"microsoft.insights/workbooks/read",
"microsoft.insights/workbooks/revisions/read",
"microsoft.insights/workbooktemplates/read"
],
"notActions": [],
"dataActions": [],
"notDataActions": []
}
],
"roleName": "Workbook Reader",
"roleType": "BuiltInRole",
"type": "Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions"
}
Workbook Reader role definition
If we analyze the
actions
property, we can see that as the description states, it grants read permissions to a few workbook-related objects. So a service-specific role that grants access to a specific service! So far so good.
Managed Applications Reader
Now, letâs check the
Managed Applications Reader
role, which its description is
âLets you read resources in a managed app

Key Points
Private sector hiring unexpectedly contracted in June, payrolls processing firm ADP said Wednesday.
It's a potential sign that the economy may not be as sturdy as investors believe.
People visit booths set up by the City of Sunrise and their police department at the Mega JobNewsUSA South Florida Job Fair at the Amerant Bank Arena on April 30, 2025 in Sunrise, Florida.
Joe Raedle | Getty Images
Private sector hiring unexpectedly contracted in June, payrolls processing firm ADP said Wednesday, in a possible sign that the economy may not be as sturdy as investors believe as they bid the
S&P 500
back up to record territory to end the month.
Private payrolls lost 33,000 jobs in June, the ADP report showed, the first decrease since March 2023. Economists polled by Dow Jones forecast an increase of 100,000 for the month. The May job growth figure was revised even lower to just 29,000 jobs added from 37,000.
"Though layoffs continue to be rare, a hesitancy to hire and a reluctance to replace departing workers led to job losses last month," Nela Richardson, ADP's chief economist, said in a press release published Wednesday morning.
To be sure, the ADP report has a spotty track record on predicting the subsequent government jobs report, which investors tend to weigh more heavily. May's soft ADP data ended up differing significantly from the
monthly jobs report figures
that came later in the week.
This week, the government's nonfarm payrolls report will be out on Thursday with economists expecting a healthy 110,000 increase for June, per Dow Jones estimates. Economists are expecting the unemployment rate to tick higher to 4.3% from 4.2%. Some economists could revise down their jobs reports estimates following ADP's data.
Weekly jobless claims data is also due Thursday, with economists penciling in 240,000. This string of labor stats comes during a shortened trading week, with the market closing early on Thursday and remaining dark on Friday in honor of the July Fourth holiday.
Service roles hit hardest
The bulk of job losses came in service roles tied to professional and business services and health and education, according to ADP. Professional/business services notched a decline of 56,000, while health/education saw a net loss of 52,000.
Financial activity roles also contributed to the month's decline with a drop of 14,000 on balance.
But the contraction was capped by payroll expansions in goods-producing roles across industries such as manufacturing and mining. All together, goods-producing positions grew by 32,000 in the month, while payrolls for service roles overall fell by 66,000.
The Midwest and Western U.S. saw the strongest contractions in June, declining by 24,000 and 20,000, respectively. Meanwhile, the Northeast shed 3,000 roles. The Southern U.S. was the sole region tracked by the ADP to see payrolls expand on net in the month, recording an increase of 13,000 positions.
The smallest firms tended to see more job losses in the month than their larger counterparts. In fact, businesses with more than 500 employees saw the biggest payroll growth in the month with an increase of 30,000, per ADP. By comparison, businesses with fewer than 20 employees accounted for 29,000 lost roles on net.
Annual income growth decreased modestly from May for both job stayers and hoppers. The rate of pay increase for those staying in their jobs ticked down to 4.4% from 4.5%, while those getting new roles slid to 6.8% from 7%.
The S&P 500 is up more than 4% for the year, posting a stunning comeback in the second quarter after worries about President
Donald Trump
's tariff fights nearly sent the benchmark into a bear market.
Clarification: The ADP report issued Wednesday referred to June data. That was not clear in an earlier version.

data.title: More assorted notes on Liquid Glass
data.author: freediver
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了苹果公司最新的用户界面 redesign，称为“Liquid Glass”，作者对其设计逻辑感到困惑。作者指出，苹果建议导航元素如标签栏和侧边栏浮动在内容层之上，以帮助用户聚焦于底层内容，但这与他们随后建议的“明确区分内容与导航元素”相矛盾。此外，增加空白区域以让内容“呼吸”被认为是不必要的，因为它减少了屏幕上显示的信息量。作者还批评了 redesign 中拉伸开关等变化，认为这些只是为了改变而改变。最后，作者对苹果的“同心设计”和“一致性”等设计指导原则的表述感到不满，认为其用词过于 pretentious 且自相矛盾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS的Liquid Glass设计语言及其相关用户界面（UI）变化的合理性和影响

不同观点：
• [cnrad] 认为Liquid Glass设计牺牲了界面的个性与乐趣，追求极简和空洞的美学，可能不利于用户体验。他希望UI设计能回归更多创意，而不是一味追求空间层次感。
• [prng2021] 质疑苹果为何会批准如此糟糕的UI变化，尤其是在用户反馈不佳的情况下。他怀疑苹果可能在赌“酷炫效果”会掩盖可用性问题。
• [hcarvalhoalves] 提出Apple可能正在为未来的VR设计铺路，通过透明的层级设计来统一UI，以便在虚拟现实中实现内容与控制的灵活布局。
• [jm4] 起初对Liquid Glass有期待，但在使用beta版后感到失望，指出按钮不清晰、低对比度文本和动画卡顿等问题，尽管如此，他仍对未来的改进抱有希望。
• [mglikesbikes] 认为尽管新设计存在可用性问题，但苹果通过这种变化为设备注入了新的生命力，特别是锁屏功能。他指出非技术用户可能不会太在意这些问题，并相信随着时间推移，设计会逐步完善。
• [cedws] 特别不喜欢圆角设计，认为在有限屏幕空间中，这种设计减少了按钮的有效点击区域，增加了视觉噪音。
• [SirMaster] 表示会立即启用“减少透明度”选项，表明对透明效果的不满。
• [a3w] 对图标设计提出批评，认为原书的图标设计更易辨识，且更符合像素丰富的屏幕显示需求。
• [erickhill] 认为Liquid Glass设计在iOS和iPadOS上可能会有不错的表现，但在macOS上可能需要多次迭代才能完善，担心新UI会影响性能。
• [_benton] 认为大多数普通用户不会太在意这些变化，认为这是“技术宅”们过度关注的问题。
• [djoldman] 认为UI变化的主要目的是销售和市场推广，而不是一致性或功能性改进，UI设计更多是在追逐潮流和新鲜感。
• [nerdjon] 讨论了第三方开发者在Apple设计语言下的困境，认为Apple通过强制统一设计来削弱第三方应用的品牌个性，但他个人支持这种做法以保持整体用户体验的一致性。

补充讨论：
• Liquid Glass设计的透明效果和空间层次感引发了对可用性和可读性问题的广泛讨论。
• 部分用户对苹果在硬件与软件美学平衡上的失策表示不满，认为新设计缺乏个性。
• 有人认为苹果可能正在为未来的VR/AR产品铺路，通过现有设计培养用户习惯。
• 尽管存在争议，部分用户仍对未来的改进抱有希望，并认为新设计能为成熟设备注入新活力。
• UI变化的商业动机也被提及，认为这种变化更多是为了市场推广和吸引新用户，而非纯粹的功能性改进。
