Key navigation elements like tab bars and sidebars float in this Liquid Glass layer to help people focus on the underlying content.
Now take a look at the area I’ve highlighted in the image. Why would you want to “focus on the underlying content” here? Tab bars and toolbars still cover the underlying content, and the more transparent/translucent they are, the worse. When something fades to the background, it literally ceases to be in the foreground, so there’s no point in focusing on it. This is like proposing an interface that helps you focus your sight on your peripheral vision.
Below the figure, in the paragraph starting with
Establish a clear navigation hierarchy
, developers are advised to:
Ensure that you clearly separate your content from navigation elements, like tab bars and sidebars, to establish a distinct functional layer above the content layer.
Which is in direct contrast to what you’ve just shown on the image above. First you propose to blur the lines between controls and content, then you advise to “clearly separate your content from navigation elements”. Which is it? If you stop and think, it’s ironic that
Ensure that you clearly separate your content from navigation elements, like tab bars and sidebars, to establish a distinct functional layer above the content layer
is the exact description of what’s happening in the ‘Before’ image!
Moving on, we get to this figure related to the
Extend content beneath sidebars and inspectors
paragraph:
In other words, create the illusion of an image that extends under a sidebar, and while you won’t actually be able to see the part of the image under the sidebar, on the other hand the transparency effect applied to the sidebar will make the text on it less legible overall. A great lose-lose situation, visually, don’t you think? Also, this might be just a matter of personal perception, but to my eyes, the blank area below the image you can see behind the sidebar looks weird, as if there’s something missing.
In
Organisation and layout
we find this:
To give content room to breathe, organizational components like lists, tables, and forms have a larger row height and padding. Sections have an increased corner radius to match the curvature of controls across the system.
Which is largely unnecessary. It reduces the amount of information displayed on screen, and you’ll have to scroll more as a consequence. Look at the Before and After layouts: the Before layout doesn’t need solutions to increase its clarity. You’re just injecting white space everywhere. It’s also ironic that where more space and ‘breathing room’ are actually necessary, the header (“Single Table Row” in the figure) is pushed even nearer to the status bar.
And don’t get me started on those redesigned, stretched-out switches. They’re the essence of ‘change for change’s sake’.
Then I went to have a look at the current
Human Interface Guidelines
and I still can’t get over that introduction:
Let’s start with
Hierarchy
: “Elevate and distinguish the content beneath them”: is this really the role of controls and interface elements? Should content and controls even occupy the same space? Should the lines be blurred between them?
In my opinion, the best way both controls and content can shine is by having each their own space: controls are out of content’s way, letting it shine and helping the user focus on it. And in their own space, controls can be clear, neatly organised, ready to be accessed in order to manipulate the content.
Next,
Harmony
:
Align with the concentric design of the hardware and software […]
No, seriously, how does one
align
in a
concentric
context? Is that a matter of picking a circle, an arc, a shape? All snark aside, this just sounds poorly worded to me. I get what Apple means here: in your app design, you should pick shapes that resemble the contours of the hardware — the shape of a MacBook’s display and bezel, for example — and the typical shapes that you find in the system’s UI. Pretty obvious stuff that’s wrapped in ‘pretentious designer vocabulary’.
Last but not least,
Consistency
:
[…] to maintain a consistent design that continuously adapts […]
The definition of
consistent
is something that is “unchanging in nature, standard,
44441279.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了苹果公司最新的用户界面 redesign，称为“Liquid Glass”，作者对其设计逻辑感到困惑。作者指出，苹果建议导航元素如标签栏和侧边栏浮动在内容层之上，以帮助用户聚焦于底层内容，但这与他们随后建议的“明确区分内容与导航元素”相矛盾。此外，增加空白区域以让内容“呼吸”被认为是不必要的，因为它减少了屏幕上显示的信息量。作者还批评了 redesign 中拉伸开关等变化，认为这些只是为了改变而改变。最后，作者对苹果的“同心设计”和“一致性”等设计指导原则的表述感到不满，认为其用词过于 pretentious 且自相矛盾。
44441279.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS的Liquid Glass设计语言及其相关用户界面（UI）变化的合理性和影响

不同观点：
• [cnrad] 认为Liquid Glass设计牺牲了界面的个性与乐趣，追求极简和空洞的美学，可能不利于用户体验。他希望UI设计能回归更多创意，而不是一味追求空间层次感。
• [prng2021] 质疑苹果为何会批准如此糟糕的UI变化，尤其是在用户反馈不佳的情况下。他怀疑苹果可能在赌“酷炫效果”会掩盖可用性问题。
• [hcarvalhoalves] 提出Apple可能正在为未来的VR设计铺路，通过透明的层级设计来统一UI，以便在虚拟现实中实现内容与控制的灵活布局。
• [jm4] 起初对Liquid Glass有期待，但在使用beta版后感到失望，指出按钮不清晰、低对比度文本和动画卡顿等问题，尽管如此，他仍对未来的改进抱有希望。
• [mglikesbikes] 认为尽管新设计存在可用性问题，但苹果通过这种变化为设备注入了新的生命力，特别是锁屏功能。他指出非技术用户可能不会太在意这些问题，并相信随着时间推移，设计会逐步完善。
• [cedws] 特别不喜欢圆角设计，认为在有限屏幕空间中，这种设计减少了按钮的有效点击区域，增加了视觉噪音。
• [SirMaster] 表示会立即启用“减少透明度”选项，表明对透明效果的不满。

• [erickhill] 认为Liquid Glass设计在iOS和iPadOS上可能会有不错的表现，但在macOS上可能需要多次迭代才能完善，担心新UI会影响性能。
• [_benton] 认为大多数普通用户不会太在意这些变化，认为这是“技术宅”们过度关注的问题。
• [djoldman] 认为UI变化的主要目的是销售和市场推广，而不是一致性或功能性改进，UI设计更多是在追逐潮流和新鲜感。

data.title: Microsoft to Cut 9k Workers in Second Wave of Major Layoffs
data.author: htrp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软大规模裁员的合理性及其背后的商业逻辑

不同观点：
• [idkwhattocallme] 认为微软在盈利丰厚且业务多样化的背景下进行大规模裁员是不合理的。他们指出，公司在过去五年中利润和估值大幅增长，裁员显得无情，且频繁的裁员让人质疑公司对员工的承诺。同时，他们提到工会可能是一个解决方案，以确保员工的工作安全。

• [shadowtree] 指出微软在印度投资30亿美元用于开发者，并大量申请H1B签证，认为这是首席执行官的 predictable behavior（可预见的行为）。这暗示了公司将资源转移至海外，可能与裁员有关。

• [crmd] 分享了其过去的工作经历，提到以前公司对员工的义务被视为最重要的，而现在的公司则通过裁员来提升股价。他们认为这种行为变得常态化，并怀疑与股票回购规则有关。

• [pseudosavant] 通过列举微软的最新季度数据（收入696亿美元，营业收入317亿美元，净利润241亿美元）来质疑裁员的必要性，指出如此高利润下裁员似乎不合理。

• [seatac76] 认为微软的Xbox部门表现不佳，导致需要缩减人员，因为其市场竞争失败和对大公司的收购使其面临困境。

• [jajuuka] 对微软裁员没有明确模式表示困惑，认为裁员没有具体依据，并质疑这种做法对士气的影响。

• [strict9] 指出在关于科技公司大规模裁员的文章中没有提到人工智能（AI），怀疑AI是否已成为裁员和外包的借口。

• [elcritch] 提到微软的生产力软件工具使用体验不佳，认为公司需要这些员工来改善产品。

• [mrtksn] 认为裁员主要集中在销售和市场部门，并提出如果AI工具有效，这些部门应能够通过AI提升市场份额。

• [nyarlathotep_] 担心裁员和外包趋势对本地住房市场的影响，特别是在西雅图这样的城市，高收入年轻人的减少可能影响房市。

• [darthplagius] 提到其在微软的朋友正在开发AI工具以提高员工生产力，但同时公司却在招聘，这显得矛盾。

补充讨论：
• 微软的投资与裁员策略之间的关系，特别是在海外市场和H1B签证上的投入，可能与本地裁员有关。
• 对AI工具在公司内部应用的质疑，以及其是否真的能替代人力。
• 裁员对员工士气和产品质量的潜在影响。
• 裁员趋势对本地经济和房市的潜在影响。

争议焦点：微软在盈利丰厚的情况下进行大规模裁员是否合理，以及这种策略是否更多地与提升股价和资源转移有关。

data.title: The Velvet Sundown are a seemingly AI-generated band with 325k Spotify listeners
data.author: ZeljkoS
data.article_summary: 《The Velvet Sundown》是一个疑似由AI生成的乐队，尽管其在Spotify上拥有超过32.5万月听众，但仅有1,533名追随者，且乐队成员在网络上几乎没有痕迹。其音乐出现在Spotify的Discover Weekly歌单中，并通过多个播放列表获得了大量听众。这些播放列表由一些神秘账户管理，包含了大量该乐队的曲目，尽管乐队与播放列表主题（如越南战争音乐）并无明显关联。此外，该乐队的音乐也被上传至Apple Music、YouTube等平台，且被Deezer识别为可能包含AI生成内容。尽管该乐队引发了广泛讨论，但目前没有确凿证据将其直接与特定AI音乐服务关联。这揭示了AI音乐在流媒体平台上悄然流行，并引发了对AI生成内容如何进入主流音乐的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成音乐的质量、影响以及在平台上的泛滥问题

不同观点：
• **showerst**认为AI生成的音乐质量目前不如人类音乐人，导致听音乐的体验受影响。他指出，尽管他习惯在工作时听音乐，但任何带歌词的音乐都会让他分心，因此他选择听随机的YouTube低保真/ chillout音乐播放列表，然而这些播放列表最近被大量AI生成的音乐充斥。他认为，虽然未来AI音乐可能会达到人类音乐人的水平，但目前质量欠佳，且很难在YouTube上区分AI生成的音乐。

• **cornhole**对AI生成的音乐持较为积极的态度。他提到自己一直在听AI Plankton制作的翻唱歌曲，并认为AI生成的声音效果 surprisingly well（出奇地好），表明他对AI音乐的接受度较高，甚至欣赏某些AI生成的作品。

• **Group_B**认为AI音乐的泛滥是不可避免的趋势，并提出质疑：如果有人 genuinely enjoys（真心喜欢）听AI生成的音乐，那还能称之为slop（劣质音乐）吗？他还关心平台如Spotify如何应对AI音乐的泛滥，以及这种趋势是否只是为了通过广告收入获利。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成音乐的质量和其对用户体验的影响。showerst认为当前的AI音乐质量不高，且难以区分，影响了用户体验；cornhole则认为某些AI生成的音乐质量不错，可以被接受和欣赏；Group_B进一步提出AI音乐是否能被称为劣质音乐的哲学问题，并关注AI音乐对平台经济的潜在影响。

• 讨论还涉及到AI音乐未来的发展趋势，尤其是其质量是否能达到人类音乐人的水平，以及如何在平台上有效管理和筛选AI生成的内容。

44442131.article_content:
Fully AI-generated music is only accounting for
a tiny proportion of streams
on services like Spotify and Deezer at the moment, and there’s an assumption in many parts of the music industry that GenAI music won’t have mainstream appeal.
Which is why it’s so interesting that a band who seem to be AI-generated have more than 325,000 monthly listeners on Spotify. And the longer you spend down the rabbit-hole of The Velvet Sundown, the more interesting it gets.
Credit where it’s due: this story begins on Reddit, with two threads this week calling attention to the band –
here
and
here
– after the music appeared in people’s Discover Weekly playlists. It was then
picked up on TikTok
by musician and author Chris Dalla Riva.
@cdallarivamusic
It was recently uncovered that A.I. generated band is getting hundreds of thousands of streams on Spotify. I break down why this is a problem.
#ai
#aimusic
#spotify
♬ original sound – Chris Dalla Riva
The facts:
The Velvet Sundown have 1,533 followers on Spotify
but 325,388 monthly listeners at the time of writing. “This four-piece band bends time, fusing 1970s psychedelic textures with cinematic alt-pop and dreamy analog soul,” explains their bio.
“Formed by vocalist and mellotron sorcerer Gabe Farrow, guitarist Lennie West, bassist-synth alchemist Milo Rains, and free-spirited percussionist Orion ‘Rio’ Del Mar, the band feels like a hallucination you want to stay lost in.”
The bio includes an approving quote from Billboard – “They sound like the memory of something you never lived, and somehow make it feel real” – which
a Google search suggests has never been published by that trade publication
.
Redditors reckon that the band photo is obviously AI, although in 2025 that could be an aesthetic decision, and have noted the lack of any online footprint for the band or its members.
No results for names as characterful as Milo Rains and Orion Del Mar – assuming Milo isn’t
this cat
– is another red flag. So Music Ally went digging.
First, this isn’t just a Spotify thing: The Velvet Sundown have music available on
Apple Music
,
Amazon Music
,
YouTube
,
Deezer
and other streaming services, although the lack of public metrics there mean we can’t tell how many listeners the band has.
However, the music being on Deezer is helpful, because that service has been developing technology to identify AI-generated music and tag it publicly. “Some tracks on this album may have been created using artificial intelligence,”
is its verdict on both of the band’s albums
.
The music being on YouTube is also helpful, because
each video’s listing reveals
that the music was “provided to YouTube by DistroKid” – meaning that this is the distributor being used by whoever’s uploading the tracks to streaming services. DistroKid’s HyperFollow tool is
also being used for smart-links to The Velvet Sundown’s music
.
So, how is the band reaching so many Spotify listeners? In his TikTok video, Dalla Riva followed the trail from the ‘Discovered On’ section of their profile, which lists the playlists where they are being found by listeners.
We’ve done that too. 25 of the top 30 playlists listed come from just four Spotify accounts:
Extra Music
,
Solitude Collective
,
KULTPOP!
,
In-between
and
Lost Records
. And this is where the rabbit-hole gets ever deeper.
Take Extra Music for example. Its profile has just under 3,000 followers, but its ‘
Vietnam War Music
‘ playlist has 629,311 saves (accounts adding it to their libraries). The 330-song playlist has tracks from a host of Vietnam War-era artists: Creedence Clearwater Revival, the Rolling Stones, Buffalo Springfield, Jimi Hendrix.
Oh, and The Velvet Sundown, whose tracks are nestled at numbers 24, 34, 43, 52, 61, 70, 79, 88, 97, 106, 115, 124, 133, 142, 151, 160, 169, 178, 187, 196, 205, 214, 223, 232, 241 and 250 in its running order. 26 tracks in all – 7.9% of the entire playlist for a band with no obvious ties to the war.
It’s a similar story for Solitude Collective. 2,002 followers but 112,609 saves for its ‘
The OC Soundtrack [All Seasons]
‘ playlist, which includes famous musical moments from the US TV show from the likes of Phantom Planet, Imogen Heap, Jeff Buckley, Oasis… and 22 tracks from The Velvet Sundown.
An impressive 13.3% of the entire playlist. Doubly impressive given that The O.C ran from 2003 to 2007, while both of The Velvet Sundown’s albums to date came out in 2025.
Like we said, it’s a rabbit-hole. A network of playlists with tens or hundreds of thousands of followers, from mysterious curator accounts, stuffed with tracks from a band who don’t appear to exist. And now that band is appearing in people’s Discover Weekly playlists.
(Yes, there is
an account called Velvet Sundown on AI-music service Suno
, but its public tracks’ titles don’t match the ones for the band on streaming services, so it’s not a proven link.)
It’s not illegal to create a virtual band, make some AI-generated music for them, upload it to streaming services via a recognised di

• **cornhole**对AI生成的音乐持较为积极的态度。他提到自己一直在听AI Plankton制作的翻唱歌曲，并认为AI生成的声音效果 surprisingly well（出奇地好），表明他对AI音乐的接受度较高，甚至欣赏某些AI生成的作品。

data.title: The Chapel Programming Language
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: Chapel编程语言是一款专注于高效并行计算的语言，适用于从个人电脑到超级计算机的各种规模。它具备生产力高、语法简洁、易读且不牺牲速度和表达能力等特点。Chapel内置支持多种并行计算模式，无需在抽象层次和低级控制之间妥协，并且能够直接在GPU上运行而无需复杂的API。文章展示了多个示例，包括分布式"Hello World"、并行文件I/O、1D热传导模拟和GPU核函数操作。Chapel已被多个项目采用，如CHAMPS多物理场模拟、Arkouda大数据分析和Coral Reef生物多样性分析，证明了其在实际生产环境中的高效性和易用性。用户反馈强调了其代码可读性和易维护性，使其特别适合教育和研究环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论中主要讨论了一种并行计算 focused 的编程语言的发展及其创新潜力，同时涉及其在高效能计算（HPC）中的应用和性能表现。

不同观点：
• [aus10d] 认为该语言聚焦于并行计算是一个重要的发展方向，并提出未来其他语言如何在这一主题上继续创新的疑问。他强调了并行计算在未来技术发展中的关键性。

• [pjmlp] 表示对该语言的长期关注，指出其在一些高性能计算中心（HPC centers）中开始流行。他还提到该语言采用了一种类似仿射类型系统（affine type system）来进行资源管理，并与其他语言进行了比较，认为该语言在生产力方面表现突出，不像Rust那么 rigid。

• [Qem] 提供了该语言在浮点基准测试中的优异表现的具体例子，引用了John Walker的网站数据，以此说明该语言在实际计算性能上的优势。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了该语言与Rust在资源管理和类型系统方面的比较，指出了两者在灵活性和生产力上的差异，这是潜在的争议点。

• 评论中也提到了具体的技术特性，如仿射类型系统在资源管理中的应用，显示了技术社区对语言设计细节的关注。

• 最后，通过引用实际的基准测试数据，[Qem] 为该语言的性能优势提供了实证支持，这在讨论中增加了技术可信度。

Try Chapel
Get Chapel
Learn Chapel
Productive
Concise and readable without compromising speed or expressive power. Consistent concepts for parallel computing make it easier to learn.
Parallel
Built from the ground up to implement parallel algorithms at your desired level of abstraction. No need to trade low-level control for convenience.
Fast
Chapel is a compiled language, generating efficient machine code that meets or beats the performance of other languages.
Scalable
Chapel enables application performance at any scale, from laptops to clusters, the cloud, and the largest supercomputers in the world.
GPU-Enabled
Chapel supports vendor-neutral GPU programming with the same language features used for distributed execution. No boilerplate. No cryptic APIs.
Open
Entirely open-source using the Apache 2.0 license. Built by a great community of developers. Join us!
Users Love It

data.title: The Evasive Evitability of Enshittification
data.author: trulyrandom
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了软件公司常面临的“劣化”问题，即产品在初期表现出色，但随着市场垄断的形成，公司为了短期收益开始降低产品质量。这种现象被称为“enshittification”，由Corey Doctorow提出。文章作者Avery认为，产品劣化并非成功的必然结果，而是源于公司对未来发展的恐惧和错误决策。成功的公司通常依赖于用户喜爱的正反馈循环，但这一循环十分脆弱，一旦公司改变战略，可能会破坏这种循环，导致产品质量下降。作者强调，控制权的变更和市场饱和是产品劣化的两大外部诱因。Tailscale承诺不会走上这条道路，并会坚守其核心价值和方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何防止软件或服务的“恶化”（enshittification）以及维持长期生存的策略

不同观点：
• ksynwa认为文章中提出的策略过于笼统和模糊，仅能得出短期内不会达到市场饱和，因此恶化不是迫在眉睫的威胁。同时对引用Google的例子感到讽刺，但仍希望作为免费用户能继续使用服务，因其对他帮助很大。

• armchairhacker指出开源是一种防御手段，但依赖竞争的防御方式可能导致另一种失败模式，即由于缺乏资源而导致的放弃或停滞。当资金耗尽时，恶化或放弃是不可避免的，除非有其他可行的方式获取资金。

• weinzierl认为文章中提到的“防御恶化”的策略不够具体，并提出可以借鉴那些数十年来避免了恶化的软件。这些软件通常具有以下特点：1. 采用copyleft许可证，2. 没有版权转让或贡献者许可协议（CLA），3. 拥有足够大且多样化的贡献者群体以使重新许可 practically impossible。此外，由501(c)(3)组织管理也是一个良好指标。

• _spduchamp质疑是否有具体的公司或产品能够避免恶化，并请求举例说明。

• juped以讽刺的口吻表示，Tailscale可能通过一个糟糕的、自嘲的名字（"tailscale"）来避免恶化，因为这会让风险投资公司失去兴趣。同时对一个实用产品还需要筹集更多资金表示怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于文章提出的策略是否有效和具体。
• weinzierl提供了基于开源软件历史的具体防御措施，并指出某些许可证和治理结构的重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及到对具体例子的需求以及对公司筹集资金动机的怀疑。

44443975.article_content:
Blog
|
insights
July 02, 2025
The evasive evitability of enshittification
This post was originally published on Avery’s personal blog as his perspective on a topic that affects nearly every software company. But because it so closely reflects the philosophy we share across the leadership and team at Tailscale — and because it captures the approach we are committed to maintaining — we’re reposting it here as an official statement of our company values and direction.
Tailscale recently
announced
our Series C fundraise. We were grateful for all the community support, but the Internet also raised a few of its collective eyebrows, wondering whether this meant the dreaded “enshittification” was coming next.
That word describes a very real pattern we’ve all seen before: products start great, grow fast, and then slowly become worse as the people running them trade user love for short-term revenue.
It’s a topic I find genuinely fascinating, and I've seen the downward spiral firsthand at companies I once admired. So I want to talk about why this happens, and more importantly, why it won't happen to us. That's big talk, I know. But it's a promise I'm happy for people to hold us to.
What is enshittification?
The term "enshittification" was first popularized in a
blog post by Corey Doctorow
, who put a catchy name to an effect we've all experienced. Software starts off good, then goes bad. How? Why?
Enshittification proposes not just a name, but a mechanism. First, a product is well loved and gains in popularity, market share, and revenue. In fact, it gets so popular that it starts to defeat competitors. Eventually, it's the primary product in the space: a monopoly, or as close as you can get. And then, suddenly, the owners, who are Capitalists, have their evil nature finally revealed and they exploit that monopoly to raise prices and make the product worse, so the captive customers all have to pay more. Quality doesn't matter anymore, only exploitation.
I agree with most of that thesis. I think Doctorow has that mechanism
mostly
right. But, there's one thing that doesn't add up for me:
Enshittification is not a success mechanism.
I can't think of any examples of companies that, in real life, enshittified because they were
successful
. What I've seen is companies that made their product worse because they were… scared.
A company that's growing fast can afford to be optimistic. They create a positive feedback loop: more user love, more word of mouth, more users, more money, more product improvements, more user love, and so on. Everyone in the company can align around that positive feedback loop. It's a beautiful thing. It's also fragile: miss a step and it flattens out and soon it's a downward spiral instead of an upward one.
So, if I were, hypothetically, running a company, I think I would be pretty hesitant to deliberately sacrifice a step from that positive feedback loop, the loop I and the whole company spent so much time and energy building, to see if I can grow faster. User love? Nah, I'm sure we'll be fine, look how much money and how many users we have! Time to switch strategies!
Why would I do that? Whenever you switch strategies, there has to be a threshold moment, when something fundamental changes.
Threshold moments and control
In
Saint John, New Brunswick, there's a river
that flows one direction at high tide, and the other way at low tide. Four times a day, gravity equalizes, then crosses a threshold to gently start pulling the other way, then accelerates. What doesn't happen is a rapidly flowing river in one direction "suddenly" shifts to rapidly flowing the other way. You can see the threshold coming. It's predictable.
In my experience, for a company or a product, there are two kinds of thresholds like this, that when crossed, create a flow change.
The first one is control: if the visionaries in charge lose control, chances are their replacements won't "get it."
The new people didn't build the underlying feedback loop, and so they don't realize how fragile it is. There are lots of reasons for a change in control; financial mismanagement, boards of directors, hostile takeovers.
The worst one is temptation. Being a founder is, well, it actually sucks. It's oddly like being repeatedly punched in the face. When I look back at my career, I guess I'm surprised by how few times per day it feels like I was punched in the face. But, the constant face punching gets to you after a while. Once you've established a great product, and amazing customer love, and lots of money, and an upward spiral, isn't your creation strong enough yet? Can't you step back and let the professionals just run it, confident that they won't kill the golden goose?
Empirically, mostly no, you can't. Actually the success rate of control changes, for well loved products, is abysmal.
The saturation trap
The second trigger of a flow change is comes from outside: saturation. Every successful product, at some point, reaches approximately all the us

• weinzierl认为文章中提到的“防御恶化”的策略不够具体，并提出可以借鉴那些数十年来避免了恶化的软件。这些软件通常具有以下特点：1. 采用copyleft许可证，2. 没有版权转让或贡献者许可协议（CLA），3. 拥有足够大且多样化的贡献者群体以使重新许可 practically impossible。此外，由501(c)(3)组织管理也是一个良好指标。

• _spduchamp质疑是否有具体的公司或产品能够避免恶化，并请求举例说明。

• juped以讽刺的口吻表示，Tailscale可能通过一个糟糕的、自嘲的名字（"tailscale"）来避免恶化，因为这会让风险投资公司失去兴趣。同时对一个实用产品还需要筹集更多资金表示怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于文章提出的策略是否有效和具体。
• weinzierl提供了基于开源软件历史的具体防御措施，并指出某些许可证和治理结构的重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及到对具体例子的需求以及对公司筹集资金动机的怀疑。

data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软（MSFT）的裁员原因及其影响，特别是与人工智能（GenAI）和股东利益的关系。

不同观点：
• AbbeFaria：作为员工和股东，AbbeFaria认为裁员是有道理的，因为公司内有些工程团队对业务贡献不大。同时，他对裁员的原因感到困惑，怀疑是否是由大股东驱动，或者是为了在生成式人工智能（GenAI）获得收入前节省资金（如GPU成本）。

• nashashmi：nashashmi认为这些裁员不是基于实际技术需求，而是“理论上”的裁员。公司文化倾向于根据需求招聘和裁员，而不是根据员工是否仍然必要。他还提到新任CEO通常会进行一些调整以观察结果，类似于“摇树”策略。

• TurkishPoptart：TurkishPoptart声称被裁员工将由持H1-B签证的AI操作人员取代，暗示外籍劳工可能填补被裁岗位。

• 1970-01-01：这位评论者认为，尽管目前AI还不能完全取代所有被裁员工，但当前情况显示出一种泡沫破裂的迹象。

• fossa1：fossa1指出，尽管公司声称AI将“增强”员工能力，但实际情况似乎是AI正在将员工挤出工作岗位。与此同时，微软的股票接近历史新高，显示出股东是裁员的受益者，而员工则是受害者。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：裁员是基于实际业务需求还是公司文化和领导层的调整策略。AbbeFaria和nashashmi对此有不同看法。
• AI在裁员和岗位替代中的角色：TurkishPoptart和fossa1提到了AI在取代员工岗位中的潜在作用，但对其当前能力和实际影响存在不同见解。
• 股东与员工利益的冲突：AbbeFaria和fossa1都提到了股东利益与员工利益之间的矛盾，特别是裁员对员工的负面影响和股东收益之间的对比。

data.author: ZenithExtreme
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于PlayStation和AMD在图形处理技术及架构方面的讨论

不同观点：
• [phkahler] 建议直接参考原文链接，以获取更多背景信息，特别是关于Sony和AMD的技术动向。
• [DiabloD3] 指出目前没有RDNA5架构，确认RDNA4是最后一个，接下来将转向UDNA1架构，并与CDNA融合。同时批评文章标题误导。
• [whatever1] 认为PS5相比PS4 Pro在性能上有显著提升，但视觉飞跃不明显，可能是图形引擎变得臃肿，或者计算能力需求大幅增加。
• [monster_truck] 强调这是AMD和Sony在FSR 3及更先进技术上的延续，特别是BVH优化方面。
• [brcmthrowaway] 提出一个对比性问题，讨论Mark Cerny和Anand Shimpi谁是更好的计算机架构师。
• [LorenDB] 表示如果PlayStation的贡献足够好，RDNA4到RDNA5的改进可能像RDNA3到RDNA4一样成功，但价格需合理。
• [erulabs] 对UDNA1的软件支持表示期待，希望能在数据中心领域与Nvidia竞争，但也担心AMD的驱动和支持问题。
• [ZenithExtreme] 简单指出AMD的下一代GPU可能包含PlayStation技术。
• [lofaszvanitt] 质疑在当前PS世代游戏稀少的情况下，新技术应用的前景。
• [shmerl] 询问Sony何时会在PS上支持Vulkan。

补充讨论：
• 技术架构和路线图的明确性是讨论的焦点，特别是RDNA和UDNA1的区别和未来发展方向。
• 对AMD驱动和软件支持的担忧反映出开发者对其历史问题的顾虑。
• PlayStation平台的游戏数量问题引发了对新技术实际应用场景的讨论。
• 关于PlayStation是否会支持Vulkan的问题也成为部分讨论者的关注点。

data.title: The Zen of Quakerism (2016)
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了贵格会（Quakerism）与禅宗佛教（Zen Buddhism）的共通之处，以及作者个人在这两种修行中的体验。作者出生于贵格会家庭，从小参加贵格会的静思会议，但一直觉得静坐困难。后来在27岁时接触到佛教，学习到禅修技巧，尤其是数息法，这帮助他更好地进行静坐。禅宗强调通过冥想实现觉醒，而贵格会则通过静默会议寻求内心和平与集体决策。两者都致力于减轻自我带来的痛苦，追求内心的和平与觉醒。作者认为这两种修行在理解自我和缓解痛苦方面都有 transformative（ transformative）的作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Quakerism的实践、特点及其与 Zen 等其他传统的比较

不同观点：
• **Quakerism的独特价值与潜在问题**：
   - **quacked** 认为Quakerism教导了对未获得权威的不尊重，但同时尊重权威本身。他强调了Quaker拒绝在《圣经》前发誓等传统，并指出现代美国Quaker社区趋于世俗化，尽管其原始目的是消除教会作为人与上帝之间的障碍。
   - **hansonkd** 指出Quaker崇拜与冥想的区别，前者强调打开心灵去“倾听”，而后者更注重正念。他还提到Quaker社区正逐渐消亡，部分原因是其缺乏信条和结构，使得新成员难以融入。他还认为Quakerism有“品牌问题”，常被误认为是Quaker燕麦或Amish。

• **Quakerism与其他神秘主义传统的联系**：
   - **mekoka** 认为Quakerism应被视为基督教神秘主义的一部分，并可以与其他神秘主义传统（如Zen、Advaita、道教、苏菲主义等）建立联系。他引用Meister Eckhart的话，指出世界各地的神秘主义者有共通之处。
   - **kmoser** 则质疑是否在Quaker会议中存在必须发言的压力，他基于自身在Quaker学校的经验，认为发言是完全自愿的，且没有必要说“灵性深刻”的话。

• **Quakerism的宗教性与非宗教性**：
   - **hermitcrab** 作为一个无神论者，表达了对Quaker在社会运动中贡献的尊重，如发起国际特赦组织、乐施会和绿色和平组织。
   - **monkeycantype** 提到自己对Quaker会议的期望与实际体验之间的差距，他原以为Quaker会对圣经持怀疑态度，但发现其与传统圣经团体相似。

补充讨论：
• **对Quakerism的误解与不了解**：
   - **bovermyer** 坦承自己对Quakerism几乎一无所知。
   - **yapyap** 和 **_benton** 都提到他们最初对Quakerism的误解，以为文章是关于电子游戏或燕麦品牌。

• **Quakerism与自然的联系**：
   - **jonaustin** 指出Quakerism和佛教都重视和尊重自然，但原文未提及这一点。

• **对Quaker会议参与方式的讨论**：
   - **gandalfian** 提到在Quaker会议中，如果感到无聊，可以看书或做其他安静的活动，强调了参与的自愿性。

• **Quakerism与Zen的比较**：
   - **antithesizer** 认为Quakerism比Zen更不“禅”，但没有详细展开。

争议焦点：
• Quaker会议中的发言是否存在压力以及Quaker社区的消亡原因存在不同看法。

44413076.article_content:
The Zen of Quakerism
February 1, 2016
By
Peter Taylor
Garden II, ink on paper, by artist and Zen Master Rebecca Nie. View more of her work at rebexart.com.
Q
uakers and Buddhists have a few things in common. Most importantly, they share a common humanity and a commitment to creating peace in the world. They are both enlightenment religions. Both George Fox and the Buddha experienced a transformative, liberating awareness through the dedicated practice of quiet contemplation.
My life is an intersection of these religions. I was born a Quaker, to Quaker parents with Quaker grandparents and great-grandparents. I attended Friends schools through college. I sat in many meetings for worship. I have always been proud to be a Quaker. I found Buddhism later in life, when I was 27 years old. I was looking for a tonic for depression. I found Buddhist philosophy and writing soothing to my condition. I liked that Buddhism talked about meditation as a remedy to suffering.
Even though I had been meditating all of my life in Quaker meetings, I had always struggled with how to do it. As a child, meeting for worship was somewhere between difficult and excruciatingly painful. To amuse myself, I would count things. I would count people with glasses. I would count ceiling tiles. I would count the seconds on my watch. I would welcome any spoken message that would break up the monotony of the silence. I would welcome the break of meeting so I could talk and run around again.
When I learned to meditate in the Buddhist style, I learned to keep my awareness focused by counting my breaths. I learned to hold my body still while I focused my mind. I found a specific place to put my hands. In meditation, I was relieved of the burden of being moved by the Spirit to speak and say something spiritually profound. Learning Buddhist meditation techniques taught me how to sit in Quaker meeting. Through all those years of Quaker upbringing and Quaker education, I had somehow missed that fundamental teaching.
In my Zen practice, I sat many hours of meditation. I did sitting meditation, walking meditation, chanting meditation, bowing meditation, eating meditation, tea-drinking meditation, and listening meditation. I went on a retreat to the Detroit Zen Center and did cooking meditation, cleaning meditation, weeding meditation, and hours and hours of sitting meditation. All that meditation was not necessarily peaceful or easy as I did it. What I found is that the rest of my days became more peaceful and easier to manage. The meditation worked. It created peace.
Besides the regular sitting practice, Zen is based on a philosophy that is different from Quakerism. Zen compelled me to practice with the enticement of an enlightenment experience. The Zen tradition is a long tradition, dating back to the Buddha (who is believed to have lived and taught between the sixth and fourth centuries B.C.E.), of purposefully awakening. Zen masters through the ages have skillfully worked with their disciples and students to create the conditions for awakening to the True Nature of reality. The push of a Zen practice is to recognize your own True Nature. The promise of that liberating experience was compelling enough to inspire me to do all that meditation.
As I studied Zen in Toronto, Ontario, I did not attend Quaker meeting. That changed when my family and I moved back to New Jersey in July 2013. Instead of finding an area Zen
sangha
(practice community), I returned to Quaker meeting for worship.
Upon returning to Quakerism, I found a group of earnest seekers, coming together in silence to try to find peace in their lives and create peace in the world. The meeting drew me into the community by inviting me to be on various committees. Committee work and the business of the meeting is one way that Quakers spread the peace of Sunday meeting for worship into the rest of the week.
In monthly meeting for business, making difficult decisions and resolving conflict test the peace of the worship. As a spiritual practice, recognizing the will of the group and releasing your own opinions can be transformative. It requires patience, respect, faith, and competent leaders to guide the process. When these factors are not present, the group may make decisions, but individuals feel excluded, egos grow, and conflict escalates. I’ve witnessed this in many meetings throughout my life. I’ve also witnessed excellent conflict resolution, where all participants feel committed to the direction of the group and uplifted through the resolution of conflict and a clear way forward.
Recognizing your True Nature in Zen and coming to a decision through Quaker process are both exercises in understanding our egos and, ultimately, easing our suffering by releasing them. This is a transformative experience that Quakerism and Buddhism offer.
In Zen, the awakening experience is a starting point for the rest of life, which will provide many more opportunities for further awakening experiences. In Quaker

data.author: justacrow
data.article_summary: 一项由瑞典卡罗林斯卡学院和中国多家医院及大学合作的新研究显示，基因疗法可以改善因OTOF基因突变导致的先天性耳聋或严重听力障碍患者的听力。研究对10名1至24岁的患者进行了治疗，使用合成腺相关病毒（AAV）将功能性OTOF基因注射到内耳。结果显示，所有患者在一个月内听力均有改善，六个月后平均可感知声音从106分贝降至52分贝。治疗安全且耐受良好，最常见的副作用是中性粒细胞减少。该研究为基因治疗耳聋开辟了新途径，未来有望应用于更多类型的遗传性耳聋。研究发表在《Nature Medicine》期刊上。

不同观点：

• [实际问题] jhaddow提出实际问题，询问如何知道自己是否患有这种类型的听力损失，尤其是对于出生以来就有听力问题的人。
• [基因技术] max_关注基因编辑技术的进展，提到CRISPR/CAS9技术，并对基因编辑股票的市场表现提出疑问。smath补充了Regeneron公司在基因疗法药物上的积极成果。
• [社会反应] d0100关注聋人社区对这种新闻的反应，并与人工耳蜗引发的争议进行比较。froggertoaster认为这种疗法可能被视为对聋人社区的生存威胁，而tribalism在争论中常常占上风。
• [伦理讨论] squigz提出了伦理问题，将听力损失治疗与自闭症治疗进行比较，质疑为何某些状况被视为需要治愈的残疾，而其他状况却被视为美丽的人性一部分。

补充讨论：
• [技术历史] UltraSane通过对比脊椎按摩疗法创始人的错误观点，强调了科学方法的力量。
• [其他需求] coolKid721幽默地提出了对治愈耳鸣的需求。

争议焦点：
• 基因疗法在听力损失治疗中的应用引发了社会和伦理层面的讨论，特别是聋人社区的反应和基因编辑技术的伦理问题。

44444626.article_content:
Published: 02-07-2025 11:00 | Updated: 02-07-2025 11:11
Gene therapy restored hearing in deaf patients
Image:
Caption:
Photo: Getty Images
Gene therapy can improve hearing in children and adults with congenital deafness or severe hearing impairment, a new study involving researchers at Karolinska Institutet reports. Hearing improved in all ten patients, and the treatment was well-tolerated. The study was conducted in collaboration with hospitals and universities in China and is published in the journal Nature Medicine.
Image:
Caption:
Maoli Duan. Photo: Ulf Sirborn
“This is a huge step forward in the genetic treatment of deafness, one that can be life-changing for children and adults,” says
Maoli Duan
, consultant and docent at the
Department of Clinical Science, Intervention and Technology
, Karolinska Institutet, Sweden, and one of the study’s corresponding authors.
The study comprised ten patients between the ages of 1 and 24 at five hospitals in China, all of whom had a genetic form of deafness or severe hearing impairment caused by mutations in a gene called OTOF. These mutations cause a deficiency of the protein otoferlin, which plays a critical part in transmitting auditory signals from the ear to the brain.
Effect within a month
The gene therapy involved using a synthetic adeno-associated virus (AAV) to deliver a functional version of the OTOF gene to the inner ear via a single injection through a membrane at the base of the cochlea called the round window.
The effect of the gene therapy was rapid and the majority of the patients recovered some hearing after just one month. A six-month follow-up showed considerable hearing improvement in all participants, the average volume of perceptible sound improving from 106 decibels to 52.
The younger patients, especially those between the ages of five and eight, responded best to the treatment. One of the participants, a seven-year-old girl, quickly recovered almost all her hearing and was able to hold daily conversations with her mother four months afterwards. However, the therapy also proved effective in adults.
“Smaller studies in China have previously shown positive results in children, but this is the first time that the method has been tested in teenagers and adults, too,” says Dr Duan. “Hearing was greatly improved in many of the participants, which can have a profound effect on their life quality. We will now be following these patients to see how lasting the effect is.”
No serious adverse reactions
The results also show that the treatment was safe and well-tolerated. The most common adverse reaction was a reduction in the number of neutrophils, a type of white blood cell. No serious adverse reactions were reported in the follow-up period of 6 to 12 months.
“OTOF is just the beginning,” says Dr Duan. “We and other researchers are expanding our work to other, more common genes that cause deafness, such as GJB2 and TMC1. These are more complicated to treat, but animal studies have so far returned promising results. We are confident that patients with different kinds of genetic deafness will one day be able to receive treatment.”
The study was conducted in collaboration with a number of institutions, including Zhongda Hospital, Southeast University, China, and was financed by several Chinese research programmes and Otovia Therapeutics Inc., the company that has developed the gene therapy and that employs many of the researchers involved in the study. See the published paper for a full list of conflicts of interest.
Publication
”AAV gene therapy for autosomal recessive deafness 9: a single-arm trial”
, Jieyu Qi, Liyan Zhang, Ling Lu, Fangzhi Tan, Cheng Cheng, Yicheng Lu, WenXiu Dong, Yinyi Zhou, Xiaolong Fu, Lulu Jiang, Chang Tan, Shanzhong Zhang, Sijie Sun, Huaien Song, Maoli Duan, Dingjun Zha, Yu Sun, Xia Gao, Lei Xu, Fan-Gang Zeng, Renjie Chai,
Nature Medicine
, online 2 July 2025, doi: 10.1038/s41591-025-03773-w.

data.title: Double is winding down
data.author: NetOpWibby
data.article_summary:
Double公司宣布将在几周内逐步停止运营，原因是客户数量不足，无法实现可持续经营。客户的资金是安全的，公司将协助将资产转移到其他券商。关键时间节点如下：

1. 7月2日起，不再接受新转入、存款或新开账户。
2. 7月30日前，自动化交易（包括清算、再平衡和税务亏损收割）将继续运行。
3. 7月31日前，客户需手动发起账户转移或清算提现。
4. 7月31日后，未关闭的账户可能需要联系Apex转移资产。

客户可通过平台发起清算并提现，或通过ACATS转移到其他券商，如M1、Wealthfront、Fidelity等。Double将承担ACATS转账费用。公司建议根据投资组合选择合适的转移目的地，并提供了相关步骤和帮助链接。对于使用定制策略的客户，推荐类似Wealthfront或Frec等平台。Double对带来的不便表示歉意，并感谢客户的支持。如有任何问题，可联系support@double.finance。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Double公司业务关闭及相关讨论

不同观点：
• jjice：对Double给出了一些资金转移的指导表示认可，但认为将资产放在创业型公司不够明智，尤其是希望退休后依赖这些资产的人。金融服务对很多人来说可能很难接受。
• ram_rar：对Double缺乏市场需求的原因感到好奇，是由于券商账户转移的摩擦，还是因为ETF已经满足了大多数零售投资者的需求？建议进行事后分析。
• xur17：计划将资产转移到Frec，并提到Apex之间的转移可以转移部分股份，同时提到使用推荐链接可以获得250美元的奖励。
• mizzao：作为Frec用户，从未听说过Double，担心Frec是否也会遇到同样的问题。
• languagehacker：解释Double的业务模式，并担心其客户在清算和转移过程中会遭受短期资本利得税的影响。
• citizenpaul：对Double的失败表示遗憾，并希望了解失败的具体原因以供学习和借鉴。
• devy：提到Double在GitHub上的许可证问题，README.md文件显示为MIT许可证，而LICENCE文件显示为GPL 3.0许可证。
• amberlyfrec：宣传Frec作为一个新的低成本直接指数提供商，并指出Frec的资产增长情况。
• infecto：分析Double失败的原因，包括市场上的竞争者、计算器的起始余额不切实际以及对高净值人群的吸引力不足。
• jvanderbot：首次听说Double这样的服务，询问HN上推荐的其他便宜的自动化投资组合管理服务。
• didip：对Double如此快就放弃感到不解。
• ramesh31：批评SEC对Double这样的公司缺乏尽职调查，导致消费者承担后果。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及Double的业务模式、市场竞争、许可证问题以及客户资产转移的实际操作和税务影响。
• 争议的焦点在于Double的失败原因以及客户在转移资产过程中可能面临的问题，特别是短期资本利得税的影响。
• 也有对其他类似服务的推荐和Frec的宣传。

总结：讨论主要围绕Double业务关闭的原因和影响展开，涉及客户资产管理、市场竞争、税务影响以及对其他服务的推荐。

44444987.article_content:
Double is winding down
JJ Maxwell
3 July 2025
(UTC)
Share this Article
To our clients,
I am writing to you today with some difficult news. We will be winding down the operations of Double in the coming weeks.
The simple reason is that we did not attract enough customers to be on a path towards building a sustainable business. In the world of investing, a company must ultimately stand on its own feet. Despite our best efforts, it has become clear that the demand for our particular low cost approach to automated portfolio investing is not sufficient to do so.
Your money is safe.
Our primary goal now is to ensure a smooth and orderly transition of your assets to another firm. You can initiate a cash withdrawal or transfer your assets to another brokerage. We ask that you do this by
July 31, 2025
. In the meantime, we will continue to operate as normal and trade within your account until July 31st, 2025. You can manually turn off trading if you’d like by going to
settings
and turning “Auto Trading Enabled” to False.
Here are the things to know:
Timeline
:
As of today July 2nd, 2025, we will no longer accept inbound transfers and deposits or new account creations.
Automated Trading on the platform, including Liquidations, Rebalancing and Tax Loss Harvesting, will continue until July 30th, 2025.
We ask that you please liquidate or initiate the outgoing transfer of your account by July 31st, 2025.
Any remaining accounts still open past July 31st, 2025 may require you to contact Apex to transfer your account out. We are exploring an automatic transfer program and will notify you as we approach this date.
After July 31st, 2025, the Double Website will have limited functionality.
How to Liquidate & Withdraw Cash
Create a Liquidation change
The next trading day, we will sell all your holdings.
You should be able to withdraw that cash to your Bank Account (
https://double.finance/transfer/withdraw
) the day after we sell your holdings.
Note there may be realized capital gains associated with liquidating your portfolio.
How to Initiate an ACATS Transfer
Turn off Automated Trading at Double by setting “Auto Trading Enabled” to False in Settings (
link
)
Open an account of the same type (Individual, Joint, Trust, RIA) at a similar brokerage firm like M1, Frec, Wealthfront, Betterment, Fidelity, Schwab, Robinhood, Public.
With your other brokerage, request a Transfer of all or part of your assets. Search for Apex Clearing, and find your account number on
the setting page within Double
. Please contact us prior to an outgoing ACATS and we will cover the outgoing $75 ACATS fee charged by Apex Clearing.
Frec
M1
Wealthfront
Betterment
Fidelity
Schwab
Interactive Brokers
Things to Note
For a Full Account ACATS Transfer, fractional holdings are generally sold and transferred as cash.
Your assets are with Apex Clearing and their DTC number is 0158
Download your Holdings in CSV format here:
https://double.finance/holdings
If you are technical
, we are
open sourcing our optimization engine
, Oracle, which does our daily Tax Loss Harvesting and rebalancing. You may be able to use this to set up your own trading bot on Alpaca. You will need to contact Alpaca support to request an ACATS of your current assets held at Double.
Note that ETF Holding data, corporate action data, and possibly factor model data would be required to reproduce Double’s Direct Index strategies. Unfortunately this data is not generally free and would require a fair bit of work to get Oracle working.
Apex Account Creation
: Create an account directly with Apex to ensure you always have access to your account documents. Here are the steps to do this:
https://help.double.finance/en/articles/10262406-how-can-i-verify-my-holdings-at-apex
Recommended Transfer Destinations
When considering where to transfer your assets, the composition of your portfolio is the key factor.
For those of you who utilized our direct indexing strategies for the S&P 500, you might consider firms like Wealthfront or Frec. They offer a similar approach with direct indexing as an option.
Different direct indexing providers have different minimums, which may impact your ability to transfer your accounts there. Frec has a $20,000 minimum for their S&P 500 strategy, compared to Wealthfront’s $5k minimum.
If you are invested in our curated "Strategies," such as the Large Market Beaters or Small Cap High Performance, you will find that brokerage firms like M1 Finance, Fidelity Basket Portfolios or Interactive Brokers provide the closest experience to Double.
Any other large brokerage like Fidelity, Charles Schwab, Robinhood, Public should be able to handle all of the assets Double holds, although they will generally not be managed/traded automatically for you.
It has been a privilege to serve you, and we are sorry for any inconvenience this shutdown may cause. We wish you all the best and can be reached at
support@double.finance
with any questions or concerns.
Sincerely,
JJ, Mark and the rest of th

data.title: MindsDB (YC W20) Is Hiring for an AI Solutions Engineer
data.author: adam_carrigan
data.article_summary: MindsDB是一家快速成长的AI初创公司，提供能够连接多种数据源并统一结构化和非结构化数据的人工智能分析解决方案。公司正在招聘一名AI解决方案工程师，负责将客户的业务问题转化为成功的生产AI解决方案。该岗位要求有五年以上面向客户的技术或解决方案工作经验，一年以上AI/ML领域工作经验，以及较强的应用开发和数据工程能力。主要职责包括与客户和产品团队沟通需求，设计和交付AI解决方案，并协助销售团队进行技术发现和解决方案设计。公司提供具有竞争力的薪酬和福利，包括弹性工作时间、健康和福利预算以及国际公司务虚活动。MindsDB是一个平等机会雇主，致力于创造多元化和包容性的工作环境。薪资范围为180,000至198,000美元。

ABOUT US
MindsDB is a fast-growing AI startup headquartered in San Francisco, California. MindsDB is an AI Analytics solution that connects to diverse data sources and applications then unifies structured and unstructured data, at petabyte scale. Powered by an industry-first cognitive engine that can operate anywhere (on-prem, VPC, serverless), it empowers both humans and AI with highly informed decision-making capabilities.
MindsDB was founded in 2017 by Adam Carrigan and Jorge Torres, inspired by Ian M. Banks's Culture series, in which super AI systems called Minds collaborate with other forms of life to accomplish incredible goals. Starting as an open source project, MindsDB now has both open source and enterprise AGI data solutions. The MindsDB community stretches across our GitHub with over 27,000 stars, nearly 800 contributors, and our Slack community of over 6,500 members from every corner of the globe and continues to grow every day.

data.title: Show HN: CSS generator for a high-def glass effect
data.author: kris-kay
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对CSS中实现玻璃效果的设计、技术及其实现细节的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• chrismorgan认为当前效果的问题在于仅模糊了紧贴表面后的像素，尤其当背景会移动时，这个问题尤为明显。如果背景是静态的，则影响不大。
• jauntywundrkind指出该效果缺乏玻璃的折射特性，这使得视觉层次感不足。Liquid Glass的强项在于通过边缘扭曲和非线性运动来增强视觉区分，而这些在静态截图中难以体现。同时，使用SVG滤镜实现这些效果非常复杂。
• magic_hamster觉得该效果不像玻璃，因为光线与斜角没有互动，且缺少光影效果。玻璃应有自身的阴影和光学效果，而不仅仅是模糊。
• mbforbes赞赏该效果，并提到在不同浏览器间的兼容性是一个额外挑战，同时好奇哪些部分最耗资源，猜测可能是backdrop-filter。
• armchairhacker指出一个小问题：当滚动时，阴影会消失，应该初始隐藏然后淡入。
• swyx分享了一些相关资源和工具，帮助快速设计和自定义玻璃效果。
• mikedelfino发现内容在手机上滚动较慢，不确定是否是玻璃效果的副作用。
• utopcell高度赞赏该项目，特别提到米纸效果很棒。
• elpocko质疑这是否是新设计，认为与2006年的Windows Vista的Aero玻璃效果相似。
• tempodox对Video标签的实现方式感到困惑。
• jand关心是否可以复制并自行托管某些资源文件。
• arfaaan和thecosas等其他用户则对该效果表示赞赏，认为它会流行于iOS设计中。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术细节，如backdrop-filter的性能问题、阴影和光影效果的实现、以及使用SVG滤镜的复杂性。
• 部分用户如elpocko对该效果的新颖性提出质疑，认为与旧有的设计（如Windows Vista的Aero玻璃效果）相似。
• 一些用户如swyx分享了相关资源和工具，帮助其他开发者实现类似的玻璃效果。
• 用户如mikedelfino和armchairhacker关注的是用户体验方面的问题，如滚动速度和界面细节。

争议焦点：
• 玻璃效果是否应包含折射和光影效果，以增强视觉层次感和真实性。
• 该设计是否具有新颖性，或仅仅是旧有设计的重新应用。

data.title: A list is a monad
data.author: polygot
data.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了函数式编程中的单子（monad）概念，指出其解释常在抽象比喻和数学抽象之间摇摆，缺乏兼具直觉和精确的描述。单子可以被视为一种容器或上下文，保存、可能包含或不包含值；也可以视为一种延迟计算的“配方”。单子编程的核心在于编写一个函数并复用于不同上下文，而无需重写控制流逻辑。

单子分为两类：“结果”单子，如`List<int>`和`Maybe<int>`，表示已计算的值及其上下文；“配方”单子，如C#的`Task<T>`，表示尚未发生的计算。

文章通过`List`和`Maybe`示例解释了`map`和`flatMap`操作，展示了单子如何管理序列化和组合，使业务逻辑保持声明式和可组合性。与面向对象和过程式编程不同，单子将控制流委托给自己，负责如何以及何时运行函数，从而简化代码。

本文为第一部分，聚焦“结果”单子，第二部分将探讨“配方”单子如`Task`的应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Monad概念及其教程的讨论

不同观点：
• brooke2k认为现有的Monad教程往往让初学者更加困惑，因为它们关注的是错误的方面。Monad本身并不复杂，建议为每种常见的Monad实例（如Maybe、IO、State等）单独授课，因为每个实例的实现和应用场景都不同。同时，Monad在Haskell中的表现更为简洁。
• gr4vityWall认为“flatMappable”是对Monad最直观的描述，而数学化的描述往往难以理解。该教程比其他文章更易懂，但在结尾部分仍然变得混乱。
• nemo1618指出列表是一个数据结构，而Monad更像是一个“trait”或“interface”。列表可以实现Monad接口，但这并不是列表本身的固有属性。Haskell的列表Monad为不确定性提供了一种模型，但这是一种选择而非唯一实现方式。
• kerblang将Monad视为解决“回调地狱”的方案，通过“do comprehensions”简化嵌套回调。Monad函数可以在任何语言中实现，但在Haskell中具有更好的可读性和“扁平化”效果。
• t43562认为过多的类比和不必要的复杂描述让Monad更难以理解，强调理解Monad的用途比了解其本质更为重要。
• robinhouston指出列表不是Monad，而是List Monad的一个实例。标题的表述对数学家来说是痛苦的。
• kelseyfrog同意robinhouston的观点，建议使用更准确的表述，如“List可以被赋予一个Monad实例”。
• 1-more解释了Monad、Applicative Functor和Functor之间的关系，并通过列表和ZipList的例子说明这些概念。
• skybrian将Monad视为一种设计模式，用于构造新对象并传递回调函数，强调Monad的“bind”操作允许嵌套回调。
• drumnerd强调Monad不是容器，而是一种组合带有效果的函数的方法，定义了如何注入值和组合函数。
• ivanjermakov认为理解Monad类似于理解OOP中类和对象的区别，强调Monad接口给实现它的类型带来的好处。
• hackandthink提到Monad作为模态的另一种视角。
• mikelitoris用幽默的方式将列表比作墨西哥卷饼。
• Smaug123认为文章没有明确指出列表作为“recipe”的最自然方式，即作为有界不确定性Monad。
• nyeah以幽默的方式建议保持数学化的讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Monad的定义和描述方式，特别是如何使初学者更容易理解。不同评论者对类比、数学化描述和具体实例的作用有不同看法。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是Monad在Haskell中的实现和表现，以及与其他语言的对比。
• 评论中还涉及Monad与其他函数式编程概念（如Functor和Applicative）的关系，通过具体例子（如ZipList）进行说明。
• 一些评论者提供了对Monad的主观理解和类比，如将其视为回调函数管理器或设计模式。

44414965.article_content:
The term “monad” is often invoked when describing patterns in functional programming. Yet explanations typically swing between high-level metaphors and deep mathematical abstractions. Each approach offers part of the picture, intuition without precision, or rigor without intuition but seldom both.
Monads can be
idealized
as a
container
(albeit is
a flawed metaphor
) or context holding a value (or multiple values, or no value),
but in some cases we will get into later on
it’s better to think of it as a
recipe
or
deferred computation
for producing a value. At the heart of monadic programming is the idea that you write
one
function, say,
f(x) = x + 1
, and then
reuse
it across different contexts without rewriting control-flow logic.
Two Flavours: Result vs Recipe
While all monads provide a computational context, they generally fall into two flavors:
Monads as “Results”: These represent a value that has already been computed, but with extra context.
List<int>
is a result with the context.
Maybe<int>
is the result of a computation with the context of “possible optionalness.” For these, the “container” metaphor is a useful, if limited, starting point.
Monads as “Recipes”: These represent a computation that has not happened yet. They are a blueprint for producing a value. C#’s
Task<T>
is a perfect example: it doesn’t hold a value, it holds the promise of a value to be computed asynchronously. For these, the “recipe” metaphor is a much better fit. Unwrapping a task doesn’t give you the computed result, it just gives you the instructions
to
compute it.
Sometimes, you can mix the flavors. In this post, we will focus on the first category to build our core intuition. We’ll start with
List
and
Maybe
to understand the mechanics of
map
and
flatMap
on concrete results. In Part 2, we’ll see how these same patterns unlock immense power when applied to “recipe” monads like
Task
.
List
: Map & FlatMap in Practice
To an OOP developer, monadic types (
List<T>
) might look just like generics. It’s a typical pitfall to think “we have generics, so we have monads,” which isn’t true by itself. Monads do usually involve generic types, but they
require specific operations (Unit and flatMap) and the three monad laws on those types to ensure uniform behavior.
This is key
and is fundamental to working with monads.
A good example of a monad is a list. You’re likely very familiar with lists and working with lists.
The monad Map operation is responsible for:
Applying your function.
For a
List
,
Map
runs
f
on
every
element, so the list
[0,1,2,3]
becomes
[1,2,3,4]
. If the list doesn’t have any elements, then, well,
Map
doesn’t call
f
.
f
doesn’t need to worry about that. Also,
f
doesn’t care if it’s a list, all
f
is, is just
f(x) = x + 1
.
Map
is responsible for running it.
Managing sequencing and combination.
The list context concatenates results into one list. We don’t need to manually modify or re-add elements to the list via
Add
.
Notice that the monad is responsible for running
f(x)
. This shift means your business logic stays
declarative
and
composable
, you describe
what
happens to a single value, and the monad describes
how
and
when
it happens.
This is different from OO and procedural programming because in procedural programming, if you want to process data, it is your responsibility to understand how to apply the function to your data. We have to use different control constructs to handle different types of data, and are also responsible for the “how”.
Here’s examples in C#:

{
return

}

data.title: ICEBlock climbs to the top of the App Store charts after officials slam it
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 美国政府官员谴责了ICEBlock应用及其媒体报道，这反而使其下载量大增，现已成为苹果App Store中排名第一的免费社交网络应用。ICEBlock由Joshua Aaron开发，旨在让用户在地图上标记ICE特工出现的位置，并添加备注，如特工的衣着或车辆。当用户靠近标记地点时，会收到提醒。白宫发言人Karoline Leavitt认为该应用可能煽动对ICE官员的暴力，ICE代理局长Todd M. Lyons则表示该应用将特工置于危险之中。美国国土安全部长Kristi Noem和司法部长Pam Bondi表示将追究Aaron的法律责任，但他强调ICEBlock不收集个人数据，且仅在iOS上可用以保护用户隐私。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一款帮助用户避开警察活动的应用程序（ICEBlock）的争议

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如neither_color）支持使用此类应用，认为这与违法行为无关，而是为了避免不必要的麻烦，如DUI检查点或交通堵塞。该用户特别提到，作为肤色较深的守法公民，不希望在非机场场所被要求出示证件并接受盘问。

• 其他用户（如datax2）将该应用与Waze、闪灯提醒等行为相提并论，认为这些都是言论自由的一部分，且在多次法庭裁决中获得支持。同时，批评某些极端言论威胁执法人员生命安全的说法。

• 一些评论（如abeppu）批评对CNN等媒体报道该应用的攻擊，认为报道或讨论如何报告警察活动本身不应被视为问题。并质疑如果讨论此类应用的文章被广泛关注，是否也意味着媒体在危害执法人员生命。

• 技术实现和平台选择成为讨论重点。一些用户（如callahad和loughy）提到苹果曾拒绝上架涉及政治敏感内容的应用，但对ICEBlock却允许上架，并讨论了在Android平台上因隐私和法律问题未能上架的情况。

• 社会经济问题也被提及（如apparent和wnevets），有用户质疑使用iOS设备的群体是否与担忧被移民执法人员拦截的群体重合，并提出是否有必要将资源用于此类应用而不是其他公共服务（如飓风卫星数据）。

• 国际对比和政治观点（如nottorp和Vektorceraptor）提到类似应用在其他国家（如伊朗）的存在，并讨论了关于移民和公共安全的意识形态分歧。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如ramoz和mandevil）提到该应用因对抗性策略而受到关注，并引用“Streisand效应”说明试图压制信息往往适得其反，增加了信息的传播。

• 也有用户（如SomeHacker44）分享了与执法人员正面互动的个人经历，提醒大家不要一概而论所有政府工作人员，但同时也认为应谨慎减少不必要的互动。

争议焦点：该应用是否构成对执法人员的威胁，及其在言论自由和隐私保护之间的平衡。此外，应用的平台选择和技术实现也引发了讨论。

US government officials have condemned ICEBlock and
CNN's
recent
coverage
of it, leading to more people hearing about its existence and downloading it from the App Store. Now the application, which allows users to add a pin on a map to show where ICE agents have recently been spotted, has
climbed
to the to the top of Apple's App Store charts. It's currently the number one free social networking app in the US and the third most downloaded free app overall.
Engadget
CNN's
piece talked about how the app's developer, Joshua Aaron, launched it in early April after seeing the Trump administration crack down on immigration. When the piece went live, Aaron said the app had 20,000 users, many of whom live in Los Angeles, where ICE has been raiding neighborhoods. In addition to letting users pin ICE agent locations on a map, the app also gives them a way to add notes, such as what the agents are wearing or what car they're driving. Any user within a five mile radius of the sighting will get an alert.
But White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt
suggested
that the
CNN
piece was "an incitement of further violence against... ICE officers" when asked to respond to the report on the podium. She said that there's been a 500 percent increase against ICE agents who are just "trying to do their jobs and remove public safety threats from... communities." ICE acting Director Todd M. Lyons also
issued a statement
, saying that the app paints a target on federal law enforcement officers' backs. "
CNN
is willfully endangering the lives of officers who put their lives on the line every day and enabling dangerous criminal aliens to evade US law," he continued. "Is this simply reckless 'journalism' or overt activism?"
ADVERTISEMENT
Advertisement
Meanwhile, US Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and US Attorney General Pam Bondi both said the government is going after Aaron. "He's giving a message to criminals where our federal officers are,"
Bondi said
. "...we are looking at it, we are looking at him, and he better watch out, because that's not a protected speech. That is threatening the lives of our law enforcement officers throughout this country."'
Aaron told
CNN
that ICEBlock doesn't collect personal data, such as device IDs and IP addresses, which
TechCrunch
has confirmed in a test. The app is only available on iOS, because it would have to collect information on Android that could put people at risk.

• 其他用户（如datax2）将该应用与Waze、闪灯提醒等行为相提并论，认为这些都是言论自由的一部分，且在多次法庭裁决中获得支持。同时，批评某些极端言论威胁执法人员生命安全的说法。

• 一些评论（如abeppu）批评对CNN等媒体报道该应用的攻擊，认为报道或讨论如何报告警察活动本身不应被视为问题。并质疑如果讨论此类应用的文章被广泛关注，是否也意味着媒体在危害执法人员生命。

• 技术实现和平台选择成为讨论重点。一些用户（如callahad和loughy）提到苹果曾拒绝上架涉及政治敏感内容的应用，但对ICEBlock却允许上架，并讨论了在Android平台上因隐私和法律问题未能上架的情况。

• 社会经济问题也被提及（如apparent和wnevets），有用户质疑使用iOS设备的群体是否与担忧被移民执法人员拦截的群体重合，并提出是否有必要将资源用于此类应用而不是其他公共服务（如飓风卫星数据）。

• 国际对比和政治观点（如nottorp和Vektorceraptor）提到类似应用在其他国家（如伊朗）的存在，并讨论了关于移民和公共安全的意识形态分歧。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如ramoz和mandevil）提到该应用因对抗性策略而受到关注，并引用“Streisand效应”说明试图压制信息往往适得其反，增加了信息的传播。

• 也有用户（如SomeHacker44）分享了与执法人员正面互动的个人经历，提醒大家不要一概而论所有政府工作人员，但同时也认为应谨慎减少不必要的互动。

争议焦点：该应用是否构成对执法人员的威胁，及其在言论自由和隐私保护之间的平衡。此外，应用的平台选择和技术实现也引发了讨论。

data.author: kotk
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了互联网内容创作和AI技术之间的变化与挑战。谷歌等搜索引擎过去通过引流为内容创作者提供价值，但随着AI工具（如ChatGPT）的兴起，用户逐渐转向AI获取答案，导致内容创作者获得的流量和收益大幅减少。文章宣布2025年7月1日为“内容独立日”，Cloudflare与多家主要出版商和AI公司合作，默认阻止未付费的AI爬虫抓取内容，确保创作者获得补偿。未来还将建立一个市场，根据内容对AI引擎的知识贡献而非流量来评估其价值，旨在促进高质量内容创作和AI发展。

44445297.article_content:
Content Independence Day: no AI crawl without compensation!
2025-07-01
Matthew Prince
4 min read
Almost 30 years ago, two graduate students at Stanford University â Larry Page and Sergey Brin â began working on a research project they called Backrub. That, of course, was the project that resulted in Google. But also something more: it created the business model for the web.
The deal that Google made with content creators was simple: let us copy your content for search, and we'll send you traffic. You, as a content creator, could then derive value from that traffic in one of three ways: running ads against it, selling subscriptions for it, or just getting the pleasure of knowing that someone was consuming your stuff.
Google facilitated all of this. Search generated traffic. They acquired DoubleClick and built AdSense to help content creators serve ads. And acquired Urchin to launch Google Analytics to let you measure just who was viewing your content at any given moment in time.
For nearly thirty years, that relationship was what defined the web and allowed it to flourish.
But that relationship is changing. For the first time in its history, the number of searches run on Google is declining. What's taking its place? AI.
If you're like me, you've been amazed at the new AI systems that have launched over the last two years and find yourself turning to them to answer questions that, in the past, you may have previously looked to Google. While it's still early, it seems clear that the interface of the future of the web will look more like ChatGPT than a spartan search box and ten blue links.
Google itself has changed. While ten years ago they presented a list of links and said that success was getting you off their site as quickly as possible, today they've added an answer box and more recently AI Overviews which answer users' questions without them having to leave Google.com. With the answer box they reported that 75 percent of queries were answered without users leaving Google. With the more recent launch of AI Overviews it's even higher.
While Googleâs users may like that, it's hurting content creators. Google still copies creatorsâ content, but over the last 10 years, because of the changes to the UI of âsearchâ it's gotten almost 10 times more difficult for a content creator to get the same volume of traffic. That means it's 10 times more difficult to generate value from ads, subscriptions, or the ego of knowing someone cares about what you created.
And that's the good news. Itâs even worse with
todayâs AI tools
. With OpenAI, it's 750 times more difficult to get traffic than it was with the Google of old. With Anthropic, it's 30,000 times more difficult. The reason is simple: increasingly we aren't consuming originals, we're consuming derivatives.
The problem is whether you create content to sell ads, sell subscriptions, or just to know that people value what you've created, an AI-driven web doesn't reward content creators the way that the old search-driven web did. And that means the deal that Google made to take content in exchange for sending you traffic just doesn't make sense anymore.
Instead of being a fair trade, the web is being stripmined by AI crawlers with content creators seeing almost no traffic and therefore almost no value.
That changes today, July 1, what weâre calling Content Independence Day. Cloudflare, along with a majority of the world's leading publishers and AI companies, is changing the default to block AI crawlers unless they pay creators for their content. That content is the fuel that powers AI engines, and so it's only fair that content creators are compensated directly for it.
But that's just the beginning. Next, we'll work on a marketplace where content creators and AI companies, large and small, can come together. Traffic was always a poor proxy for value. We think we can do better. Let me explain.
Imagine an AI engine like a block of swiss cheese. New, original content that fills one of the holes in the AI engineâs block of cheese is more valuable than repetitive, low-value content that unfortunately dominates much of the web today.
We believe that if we can begin to score and value content not on how much traffic it generates, but on how much it furthers knowledge âÂ measured by how much it fills the current holes in AI engines âswiss cheeseâ â we not only will help AI engines get better faster, but also potentially facilitate a new golden age of high-value content creation.
We donât know all the answers yet, but weâre working with some of the leading economists and computer scientists to figure them out.
The web is changing. Its business model will change. And, in the process, we have an opportunity to learn from what was great about the web of the last 30 years and what we can make better for the web of the future.

data.title: Firefox 120 to Firefox 141 Web Browser Benchmarks
data.author: mikece
data.article_summary: 本文由Michael Larabel撰写，比较了从2023年11月的Firefox 120到最新的Firefox 140稳定版及141测试版的性能。所有测试在同一台运行Ubuntu Linux系统的AMD Ryzen 9 9950X处理器设备上进行，评估了浏览器的性能和内存使用情况。由于Firefox 119及之前版本在自动化测试中遇到问题，测试从Firefox 120开始。每个主要版本都进行了多种基准测试，并监测了内存使用情况。测试使用的是Ubuntu 25.04系统，以确保一致性。结果展示了Firefox在过去近两年中的性能变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：浏览器的性能、功能、用户体验及相关问题

不同观点：
• **支持Firefox**：
   - **saubeidl**：Firefox表现不错，Mozilla不像Google那样“邪恶”，浏览器垄断对任何人都没有好处。Firefox继续支持Manifest v2，uBlock等插件能正常工作，是切换浏览器的好时机。
   - **cadamsdotcom**：Firefox非常优秀，特别是在Mac上，支持adblock且有助于防止浏览器单一化。
   - **alberth**：浏览器之间的电池寿命差异也不再显著，Firefox表现均衡。

• **浏览器性能讨论**：
   - **em500**：尽管浏览器和硬件速度变快，但实际使用中由于复杂的网页框架、认证墙和广告，用户体验并没有显著提升，符合Wirth定律和Jevons悖论。
   - **Night_Thastus**：现代PC上浏览器性能差异不大，瓶颈往往是网页而不是浏览器。移动端浏览器的体验较差，尤其是面对广告和慢速网站。
   - **Milpotel**：慢速主要源于网站和网络连接，而非浏览器本身。

• **浏览器体验问题**：
   - **butz**：安装广告拦截器是提升网页性能的最佳方法。
   - **blinding-streak**：引用测试数据，Firefox 141 Beta比120版本快12%。

• **Firefox的缺陷与批评**：
   - **taf2**：除非Mozilla解决某些长期存在的问题，否则不接受Firefox，认为其已经失去原有价值。
   - **amendegree**：批评Firefox的更新过程繁琐，需要手动确认UAC提示且中断当前浏览。

补充讨论：
• **浏览器与广告**：评论中多次提到广告和广告拦截器对浏览体验的影响，尤其是移动端。
• **特定网站问题**：例如**chrisweekly**提到Phoronix网站的用户体验差，Reader模式下仍有广告问题。
• **浏览器选择动机**：部分评论强调了隐私、防止垄断以及对开源软件的支持是选择Firefox的重要理由。

Firefox 120 To Firefox 141 Web Browser Benchmarks
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Software
on 2 July 2025 at 11:00 AM EDT.
Page 1 of 5
.
11 Comments
.
For those curious about the direction of Mozilla Firefox web browser performance over the past year and a half, here are web browser benchmarks for every Firefox release from Firefox 120 in November 2023 through the newest Firefox 140 stable and Firefox 140 beta releases from a few days ago. Every major Firefox release was benchmarked on the same Ubuntu Linux system with AMD Ryzen 9 9950X for evaluating the performance and memory usage of this open-source web browser.
Following the recent
Firefox 141 beta benchmarks looking at the lower RAM usage
on Linux, I got carried away and decided to benchmark every Firefox release going back to Firefox 120 that debuted in November of 2023. Firefox 120 was the breaking point since Firefox 119 and prior ended up running into issues with Selenium / Gecko web driver for automating the benchmarks. So due to that breakage, Firefox 120 was the old cut-off but still a useful exercise in seeing the performance of Firefox on Linux over roughly the past nearly two years.
The release builds of every major Firefox release from Firefox 120 through Firefox 141 Beta were tested. In the case of Firefox 125, Firefox 125.0.1 was used since Firefox 125.0 binaries were removed due to problems. In addition to looking at the Firefox performance across a variety of web browser benchmarks, the RAM usage was also monitored for reference.
The same AMD Ryzen 9 9950X desktop system running Ubuntu 25.04 was used for collecting all of these fresh Mozilla Firefox web browser benchmarks. The testing is very straight-forward so let's get right to it.

data.title: Stop Killing Games
data.author: MYEUHD
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频游戏软件的终止支持及其对消费者的影响，如何立法规范以保障消费者权益，以及该问题是否仅限于游戏行业。

不同观点：
• **支持对消费者保护的立法**：andrecarini认为需要立法来防止消费者在购买软件后因服务终止而受损，并提出了几种可能的解决方案，如设置软件到期日、公开服务器源代码或允许反向工程。icu和butlike等用户也支持这种立法，认为需要对消费者提供更多保护，并强调行业内存在许多不利于消费者的行为。

• **质疑立法如何执行**：Apreche和jasonthness对立法的可行性提出质疑。Apreche指出，如果公司破产，无法强制其维持服务器运行，且强制公开代码可能涉及其他知识产权问题。jasonthness认为法律无法凭空产生资金或维持运营的意愿，并担心法规会伤害独立开发者。

• **对多玩家游戏的特殊性存在争议**：hombre_fatal和royal__讨论了多玩家游戏的特殊性。hombre_fatal认为多玩家游戏在何时应退款的问题上不明确，且与单人游戏不同。royal__指出，无法预测游戏的长远成功，服务器成本是主要问题，尤其是在MMOs中。

• **现有解决方案的实例**：VonGuard提到在美国已有通过DMCA豁免允许单人游戏在服务器关闭后继续运行的案例，展示了现有的一些法律途径。ortusdux提供了ACEmulator作为MMORPGs的社区支持解决方案实例。

• **对整个软件行业的扩展讨论**：arandomhuman认为该问题不仅限于游戏行业，而是广泛存在于一次性购买的软件许可模型中，主张软件供应商应对产品终止支持负有责任。

补充讨论：
• **DRM和社区解决方案**：lousken强调使用无DRM和具备专用服务器/局域网选项的重要性。
• **立法对创新的潜在影响**：Derelicte提到像《Pokémon Go》这样的游戏可能无法在强制立法下诞生，暗示立法可能抑制创新。

总体来看，讨论围绕消费者保护、立法可行性、多玩家游戏的特殊性以及现有和潜在解决方案展开。争议焦点在于如何在保护消费者权益和不损害开发者利益之间取得平衡。

data.title: Ask HN: Who is hiring? (July 2025)
data.author: whoishiring
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多个科技公司发布的招聘信息及其对候选人的要求

不同观点：
• Estuary强调其开放源代码和开发者优先的文化，专注于实时数据基础设施，寻找具有后端工程经验并能处理复杂API和数据库集成的工程师。
• kierangill介绍Blueberry Pediatrics的使命——通过提供负担得起的、高质量的小儿远程医疗服务来改变美国医疗保健。他们寻找全栈工程师，重视全栈知识、好奇心和强大的工作 ethic。
• camperegrine展示Peregrine Technologies的工程团队，帮助关键机构通过解锁数据价值来改善运营。他们正在寻找具有丰富经验的高级软件工程师，尤其是在AI和基础设施方面。
• katyborrowell描述Borrowell作为加拿大金融科技公司的领先地位，正在寻找开发人员加入其团队，强调多样性、包容性和创新文化。
• manish_gill介绍ClickHouse的招聘需求，特别是云基础设施和Kubernetes方面的专业知识，要求候选人具备独立和自组织的能力。
• mstubna介绍Hackensack Meridian Health的招聘信息，寻找高级软件工程师和数据科学家，帮助构建数据管道和AI解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 各公司对技术栈有不同的偏好，例如Estuary偏好Go和Rust，Blueberry Pediatrics使用Django和Flutter，Peregrine Technologies使用React和Kafka，Borrowell偏好全栈开发和测试自动化。
• 工作地点和形式多样，包括远程工作（如Estuary、Blueberry Pediatrics、Borrowell）、混合模式（如Peregrine Technologies、Coveo）以及特定地点要求（如Calico在波士顿，MONUMENTAL在阿姆斯特丹）。
• 对候选人的期望不仅限于技术能力，还包括沟通能力、团队合作、自主性和创新精神（如Goody、Coveo、Peregrine Technologies）。
• 某些公司强调其初创环境和快速发展机会，如Estuary、Goody、Yottar和Monumental，这些公司提供高自主性和股权激励。

争议焦点：
• 不同公司对远程工作的接受程度以及对技术栈的偏好可能成为候选人选择公司的争议点。例如，一些公司完全接受远程工作（如Estuary、Blueberry Pediatrics），而另一些公司则更倾向于混合模式（如Peregrine Technologies、Coveo）。
• 对于某些角色，如AI工程师和云架构师，不同公司提供的薪酬范围和股权激励可能成为吸引候选人的竞争点。

总结：
上述评论展示了多家科技公司在招聘高级软件工程师和其他相关职位时的不同要求和公司文化。这些公司不仅关注技术能力，还重视候选人的沟通能力、团队合作和自主创新精神，提供了多样化的工作地点和形式选择。

data.title: Three Ubisoft chiefs found guilty of enabling culture of sexual harassment
data.author: freddier
data.article_summary: Ubisoft三名高管被判建立并助长职场性骚扰和心理骚扰文化，其中包括公司前创意总监Serge Hascoët。法院发现Hascoët犯有心理骚扰和共谋性骚扰罪，被判18个月缓刑及罚款€45,000。另一名前高管Thomas François被判性骚扰、心理骚扰及 attempted sexual assault，获三年缓刑及罚款€30,000。前游戏总监Guillaume Patrux也被判心理骚扰，获12个月缓刑及罚款€10,000。证词显示，Ubisoft巴黎办公室在2012至2020年间存在严重的性别歧视和不当行为，被形容为“法外男士俱乐部”。此案被视为游戏行业#MeToo运动的重要转折点。Hascoët考虑上诉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对涉及性骚扰和虐待事件的报道和标题的准确性及其背后的历史背景。

不同观点：
• [mmonaghan] 认为文章的标题不够准确，建议标题应更直接地反映事件的严重性。他强调，这不仅仅是“男孩间的胡闹”，而是实际的虐待行为，读者应该通过阅读文章来了解事件的严重性。

• [burnt-resistor] 则提到了类似事件在历史上未被曝光的现象，特别是Sun Microsystems在过去几十年中的严重虐待行为未被公开报道，暗示这类问题长期存在但未得到应有的关注。

补充讨论：
• [mmonaghan] 强调事件的严重性，并认为媒体有责任通过准确的标题来传达这种严重性。

• [burnt-resistor] 提到了历史上的类似事件，指出社会和媒体在过去对这类问题的忽视，暗示当前的报道可能是一种进步，但也反映出过去的不公正。

争议的焦点：
• 标题的准确性和媒体责任：[mmonaghan] 认为当前标题未能反映事件的严重性，而 [burnt-resistor] 则关注历史上类似事件未被曝光的现象。

• 事件严重性的认知：[mmonaghan] 明确指出这是实际的虐待行为，而非简单的“男孩间的胡闹”，而 [burnt-resistor] 的评论则暗示了这种行为在历史上长期被忽视的问题。

Three Ubisoft chiefs found guilty of enabling culture of sexual harassment
Former staff likened offices of video game company in Paris to a ‘boys’ club above the law’
Angelique Chrisafis
in Paris
Wed 2 Jul 2025 11.12 EDT
First published on Wed 2 Jul 2025 11.11 EDT
Share
Three former executives at the video game company
Ubisoft
have been given suspended prison sentences for enabling a culture of sexual and psychological harassment in the workplace at the end of the
first big trial
to stem from the
#MeToo movement
in the gaming industry.
The court in Bobigny, north of Paris, had heard how the former executives used their position to bully or sexually harass staff,
leaving women terrified
and feeling like pieces of meat.
Former staff had said that between 2012 and 2020, the company’s offices in Montreuil, east of
Paris
, were run with a toxic culture of bullying and sexism that one worker likened to a “boys’ club above the law”.
Former bosses at video games firm Ubisoft on trial in France accused of sexual harassment
Read more
Ubisoft is a French family business that rose to become one of the biggest video game creators in the world. The company has been behind several blockbusters including
Assassin’s Creed
,
Far Cry
and the children’s favourite
Just Dance
.
The state prosecutor, Antoine Haushalter, had told the court the world of video games and its subculture had an element of “systemic” sexism and potential abuse and called the trial a “turning point” for the gaming world.
Thomas François, 52, a former
Ubisoft
editorial vice-president, was found guilty of sexual harassment, psychological harassment and an attempted sexual assault. He was given a three-year suspended prison sentence and fined €30,000 (£26,000).
The court heard how he once tied a female member of staff to a chair with tape, pushed the chair into a lift and pressed a button at random. He was also accused of forcing one woman wearing a skirt to do handstands.
She told the court: “He was my superior and I was afraid of him. He made me do handstands. I did it to get it over with and get rid of him.”
View image in fullscreen
Thomas François, a former Ubisoft editorial vice-president, was found guilty of sexual harassment, psychological harassment and an attempted sexual assault.
Photograph: Xavier Galiana/AFP/Getty
At a 2015 office Christmas party with a Back to the Future theme, François allegedly told a member of staff that he liked her 1950s dress. He then allegedly stepped towards her to kiss her on the mouth as his colleagues restrained her by the arms and back. She shouted and broke free.
François had told the court there was a “culture of joking around”. He said: “I never tried to harm anyone.”
Serge Hascoët, 59, Ubisoft’s former chief creative officer and second-in-command, was found guilty of psychological harassment and complicity in sexual harassment.

He was acquitted of sexual harassment and complicity in psychological harassment. He was given an 18-month suspended sentence and a fine of €45,000.
The court heard he once handed a young female member of staff a tissue in which he had blown his nose, saying: “You can resell it, it’s worth gold at Ubisoft.” The court heard that Hascoët bullied assistants by making them carry out personal tasks for him such as going to his home to wait for parcel deliveries.
Hascoët had told the court he was unaware of any harassment, saying: “I have never wanted to harass anyone and I don’t think I have.”
Hascoët’s lawyer, Jean-Guillaume Le Mintier, said his client was considering an appeal.
The former Ubisoft game director, Guillaume Patrux, 41, was found guilty of psychological harassment and given a 12-month suspended sentence and a fine of €10,000.
The court heard he had punched walls, mimed hitting staff, cracked a whip near colleagues’ faces, threatened to carry out an office shooting and played with a cigarette lighter near workers’ faces, setting alight a man’s beard. He had denied the charges.

data.title: Automatically Rewrite Container Image References in Kubernetes
data.author: flemzord
data.article_summary:
**Mutating Registry Webhook** 是一个 Kubernetes 可变准入 Webhook，用于自动重写容器镜像引用，使其使用缓存注册表（如 AWS ECR Pull Through Cache）。它支持基于正则表达式和命名空间/标签的重写规则，适用于将镜像从 Docker Hub、GCR、Quay.io 等重定向到内部注册表。该项目具有高性能、安全性（通过 cert-manager 集成）、Prometheus 指标支持和 Helm 图表部署等特性。

**快速开始**：
1. 安装 cert-manager。
2. 使用 `kubectl apply` 安装 Webhook。
3. 创建 `RegistryRewriteRule` 自定义资源以定义重写规则。
4. 构建并推送镜像，部署到集群。

项目提供 YAML 文件和 Helm 图表两种部署方式，便于用户安装和分发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在Kubernetes和容器运行环境中处理镜像注册的地址重写方案，特别是在内部网络或隔离环境（air-gapped environments）中的应用。

不同观点：
• [sscarduzio] 认为可以在内部网络中运行注册表并使用重写规则，帮助解决隔离环境中的镜像获取问题。不过，他询问是否存在潜在的“陷阱”或问题。

• [remram] 提出另一种思路，建议将重写规则直接构建到容器运行时的配置中，而不是仅仅依赖自动重写。他认为即使自动重写了镜像地址，但在通过API服务器读取时，重写后的镜像仍然可见，这可能不是理想的方案。

• [flemzord] 分享了自己的实际经验，表示已经开发了一个Kubernetes的Mutating Admission Webhook，可以在Pod创建和更新时自动根据配置规则重写镜像引用。这种方法可以有效地将公共注册表的镜像重定向到内部镜像或缓存，从而提高安全性和可靠性。

• [nonameiguess] 则指出可以使用containerd的注册表镜像功能来实现相同的效果，并且重写规则的语法是一样的，认为没有必要额外开发其他工具或配置。

补充讨论：

Mutating Registry Webhook
A Kubernetes mutating admission webhook that automatically rewrites container image references to use pull-through cache registries (like AWS ECR Pull Through Cache).
Description
This webhook intercepts Pod creation and update requests in your Kubernetes cluster and automatically rewrites container image references based on configurable rules. This is particularly useful when you want to:
Use AWS ECR Pull Through Cache to reduce external registry dependencies
Implement a corporate image proxy/cache
Redirect images from Docker Hub, GCR, Quay.io, or other registries to your internal registry
Apply different rules based on namespaces or pod labels
Features
🔄 Automatic image URL rewriting based on regex patterns
🎯 Namespace and label-based targeting
⚡ High-performance with in-memory rule caching
🔒 Secure by default with cert-manager integration
📊 Prometheus metrics support
🎛️ Helm chart for easy deployment
🧪 Comprehensive test coverage
Getting Started
Prerequisites
go version v1.24.0+
docker version 17.03+
kubectl version v1.11.3+
Access to a Kubernetes v1.11.3+ cluster
cert-manager v1.0+ installed in your cluster
Quick Start
Install cert-manager
(if not already installed):
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.13.0/cert-manager.yaml
Install the webhook
:
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/flemzord/mutating-registry-webhook/releases/download/v0.2.0/install.yaml
Create a RegistryRewriteRule
:
apiVersion
:
dev.flemzord.fr/v1alpha1
kind
:
RegistryRewriteRule
metadata
:
name
:
docker-hub-to-ecr
spec
:
rules
:
#
Redirect Docker Hub images to ECR pull-through cache
-
match
:
'
^docker\.io/(.*)
'
replace
:
'
123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dockerhub/$1
'
#
Handle images without explicit registry (defaults to docker.io)
-
match
:
'
^([^/]+/[^/]+)$
'
replace
:
'
123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dockerhub/$1
'
To Deploy on the cluster
Build and push your image to the location specified by
IMG
:
make docker-build docker-push IMG=
<
some-registry
>
/mutating-registry-webhook:tag
NOTE:
This image ought to be published in the personal registry you specified.
And it is required to have access to pull the image from the working environment.
Make sure you have the proper permission to the registry if the above commands don’t work.
Install the CRDs into the cluster:
make install
Deploy the Manager to the cluster with the image specified by
IMG
:
make deploy IMG=
<
some-registry
>
/mutating-registry-webhook:tag
NOTE
: If you encounter RBAC errors, you may need to grant yourself cluster-admin
privileges or be logged in as admin.
Create instances of your solution
You can apply the samples (examples) from the config/sample:
kubectl apply -k config/samples/
NOTE
: Ensure that the samples has default values to test it out.
To Uninstall
Delete the instances (CRs) from the cluster:
kubectl delete -k config/samples/
Delete the APIs(CRDs) from the cluster:
make uninstall
UnDeploy the controller from the cluster:
make undeploy
Project Distribution
Following the options to release and provide this solution to the users.
By providing a bundle with all YAML files
Build the installer for the image built and published in the registry:
make build-installer IMG=
<
some-registry
>
/mutating-registry-webhook:tag
NOTE:
The makefile target mentioned above generates an 'install.yaml'
file in the dist directory. This file contains all the resources built
with Kustomize, which are necessary to install this project without its
dependencies.
Using the installer
Users can just run 'kubectl apply -f ' to install
the project, i.e.:
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/
<
org
>
/mutating-registry-webhook/
<
tag or branch
>
/dist/install.yaml
By providing a Helm Chart
Build the chart using the optional helm plugin
kubebuilder edit --plugins=helm/v1-alpha
See that a chart was generated under 'dist/chart', and users
can obtain this solution from there.
NOTE:
If you change the project, you need to update the Helm Chart
using the same command above to sync the latest changes. Fu

data.title: 14 Million People Could Die in Next 5 Years Due to USAID Cuts, Study Finds
data.author: perihelions
data.article_summary: 一篇发表于2025年7月1日的文章指出，埃隆·马斯克和特朗普政府通过其效率部门（DOGE）对美国国际开发署（USAID）的大幅削减资金，可能导致未来五年内全球1400万人本可避免的死亡，其中包括450万名五岁以下儿童。USAID自2001年以来通过资助拯救了约9100万人的生命，尤其在对抗艾滋病、疟疾和被忽视的热带疾病方面成效显著。研究警告，若不恢复资金，到2030年将出现大量额外死亡。尽管USAID存在一些问题，如阿富汗的资金欺诈指控，但它在全球公共卫生方面总体上起到了积极作用。马斯克和特朗普的行动被批评为对全球最脆弱地区的健康构成严重威胁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国国际开发署（USAID）资金削减的影响以及资金来源的争议

不同观点：
• **反对使用纳税人资金支持USAID**：tracker1认为，USAID的资金削减应该由慈善捐款来填补，他根本上反对使用纳税人的钱进行对外援助，认为慈善可以减少官僚主义，更直接地帮助有需要的人。

• **质疑USAID的有效性和目的**：FilosofumRex指出，USAID的资金更多用于满足西方精英的偏好，而不是当地政府的实际需求，因此其削减可能会导致更多死亡，但这也暗示了USAID本身可能并非完全有效。

• **批评私人慈善家的作用**：more_corn以讽刺的口吻批评像比尔·盖茨这样的超级富豪，认为他们的影响力可能导致了更多的不必要死亡，暗示私人慈善并不能完全替代政府援助。

• **支持私人慈善填补资金缺口**：TurkishPoptart认为，像比尔·盖茨这样的私人慈善家有能力填补USAID资金削减带来的缺口，并指出即使这样做了，私人慈善家仍然会剩下大量财富。

• **对报道的质疑和讽刺**：hulitu对有关“1400万人可能因USAID削减而死亡”的报道持怀疑态度，甚至将其与讽刺新闻网站The Onion相提并论，暗示这种预测可能过于夸张。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于USAID资金的有效性、使用目的以及是否应由慈善代替政府拨款。一部分人认为私人慈善更有效，而另一部分人则质疑私人慈善的可靠性和广泛性。

• 对媒体报道的可靠性也有不同看法，有人认为这种预测过于夸张，可能是为了引起公众关注。

A protester outside of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) headquarters holds a sign with an anti-DOGE message

Elon Musk’s wood-chipping of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) is poised to leave piles of bodies behind in its wake, a new study suggests. Scientists have calculated that recent funding cuts to USAID could lead to millions of preventable deaths worldwide over the next half-decade.
An international group of researchers conducted the study,
published
Monday in the Lancet. They estimated that USAID funding in developing countries has helped save dozens of millions of lives since 2001, while the drastic cuts dictated by Musk and his Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) could contribute to 14 million deaths in the next five years, including many children under 5 years old.
“Our estimates show that, unless the abrupt funding cuts announced and implemented in the first half of 2025 are reversed, a staggering number of avoidable deaths could occur by 2030,” the researchers wrote.
The renewed Trump administration has gutted many crucial government agencies and departments since January, including the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. But perhaps none of the cuts have been as vicious as those to the USAID, the agency primarily in charge of distributing the country’s foreign aid.
Though the USAID certainly has its blemishes (government watchdogs have
alleged
that its funding contributed to widespread fraud during America’s occupation of Afghanistan, for instance), it’s been a net positive for global public health. USAID resources have bolstered programs throughout the world to provide people vaccines, anti-malaria mosquito nets, and other vital medical supplies. One particular USAID-operated initiative, the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), is
estimated
to have prevented over 5 million children from being born with HIV.
Unelected Billionaire Elon Musk Is Shutting Down the Government Agency USAID
Musk and others within the Trump White House seemed to take a perverse joy in sabotaging the USAID through widescale cuts and layoffs. In early February, Musk
bragged
on X that he had “spent the weekend feeding USAID into the wood chipper.” While USAID employees have
challenged
these layoffs in court, arguing they were illegal and unconstitutional, the agency remains critically underfunded and shorthanded.
The study researchers first looked back at the life-saving impact that USAID funding has had globally, then projected how the current loss of resources will change things moving forward. Based on data from over 130 countries, they estimated that USAID funding had likely saved 91 million lives between 2001 and 2021, with the largest reductions in mortality tied to HIV/AIDS, malaria, and neglected tropical diseases. They also forecasted that the DOGE-mandated cuts will result in 14 million preventable deaths by 2030, including 4.5 million deaths of children under 5.
âOur analysis shows thatÂ USAID funding has been an essential force in saving livesÂ and improving health outcomes in some of the worldâs most vulnerable regionsÂ over the past two decades,â said lead author Daniella Cavalcanti, a postdoctoral researcher at the Federal University of Bahia’s Institute of Collective Health in Brazil, in a
statement
. Scientists from the Barcelona Institute for Global Health in Spain and the University of California, Los Angeles, also contributed to the study.
Trump’s ‘Big Beautiful Bill’ Will Literally Kill, Study Warns
Musk is no longer officially part of President Donald Trump’s inner circle, his designation as a special government employee having run out in
late May
. And after a brief ceasefire, he and Trump have continued to
throw barbs
at each other over the GOP’s Big Beautiful Bill (which itself may lead to many
preventable deaths
from Medicaid cuts). But DOGE and many of the cuts it’s implemented continue to endure. Other
recent
reports
from aid groups indicate that people are already dying as a result of these funding losses.
Unless things change dramatically, Musk’s legacy will be one stained with the blood of the poor and vulnerable.

data.author: mmarian
data.article_summary: 伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安宣布，德黑兰已暂停与国际原子能机构（IAEA）的合作，这是在美国6月21日对其核设施进行打击后采取的重大举措。伊朗议会于7月25日通过法案，冻结与IAEA的合作，具体内容尚不明确，但国家媒体称IAEA检查员需获得伊朗最高国家安全委员会批准才能访问核设施。伊朗还禁止IAEA总干事拉斐尔·格罗西访问其核设施，并拆除了监控摄像头，引发英法德三国谴责。美国总统特朗普称美军袭击“彻底摧毁”了伊朗设施，但格罗西评估损害并非“彻底”。格罗西警告伊朗可能在“数月内”重新生产浓缩铀，伊朗官员则批评其未谴责袭击。伊朗曾在2015年核协议中允许IAEA检查，但美国2018年退出该协议。
